items.title: Fashola says election riggers deserve jail, not death
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has said people who manipulate election results should face imprisonment rather than execution, urging Nigerians to reject violent rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. Fashola made the remarks during a television interview on Friday while reacting to the “rig and die” statement attributed to Ovie Omo-Agege, a Delta Central senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress. The former Minister of Works and Housing said electoral offences must be punished under the law, arguing that even where an offence attracts capital punishment, the accused must first be charged, tried and given an opportunity to defend themselves. “Absolutely not. I mean, come on. I think we must move away from what I think are extreme narratives and rhetoric,” Fashola said when asked whether election riggers should be killed. He stressed that the Electoral Act does not prescribe death as punishment for election rigging. “The punishment under the Electoral Act is not death. And even if it were death, which I will not support, there’s a process before you take human life; a charge, a trial, an opportunity to defend yourself,” he said. Fashola, however, maintained that election manipulation should attract serious punishment and urged politicians to seek votes through legitimate campaigns. “The penalty for rigging is not death. But don’t rig. Go and campaign for your party,” he added. He advised political parties to concentrate on mobilising voters in areas where they enjoy support rather than attempting to manipulate results in places where they have little electoral influence. The former governor also advocated stiffer prison sentences for serious electoral offences, suggesting that some violations should carry custodial penalties without the option of a fine. “I think maybe there might be stiffer sentences without the option of a fine, maybe a defined custodial sentence that is deterrent in nature,” he said. Fashola further called for greater public education on electoral conduct, noting that Nigeria had repeatedly amended its electoral laws without giving sufficient attention to educating citizens about the principles of democracy. He said sustained nationwide enlightenment would help reduce desperation during elections and encourage politicians and voters to understand that electoral contests could produce either winners or losers. The post Fashola says election riggers deserve jail, not death appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Makkah Defence Alliance meeting in Islamabad begins with Yemen conflict also on agenda
items.description: A meeting of the tripartite Makkah Defence Alliance’s top decision-making body has begun in Islamabad, with discussions also expected to feature the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi fighters in Yemen. The third session of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) is being held in the federal capital, where authorities have announced a public holiday today and imposed special movement restrictions in view of the high-level gathering. A local holiday has also been announced in Rawalpindi. The SPDC comprises the foreign and defence ministers and top military officials of the three countries. The Islamabad meeting is expected to focus on finalising standard operating procedures (SOPs), establishing an implementation mechanism and defining coordination between the three countries’ political, defence and military institutions, a Pakistani official said. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said on Thursday that the foreign and defence ministers of Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan would participate in the meeting and the “continuous turmoil south of Saudi Arabia will obviously be one agenda point in the meeting”. “It is very important,” he remarked. Saudi Arabia has faced repeated attacks by Yemen’s Ansar Allah movement, commonly known as the Houthis, targeting cities, oil facilities and shipping since fighting in Yemen’s civil war intensified in July. “Any threat to Saudi Arabia is a threat to Pakistan and Turkiye according to the pact, which is absolutely clear,” Asif said. The alliance The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on Aug 7. The pact provides that an armed attack on any one member will be considered an attack on all, obliging the other two to extend assistance through available means, including military support. The SPDC, which brings together the foreign and defence ministers and chiefs of defence staff of the three countries, is the alliance’s principal decision-making forum. A permanent secretariat has been established in Riyadh to coordinate its work, with Pakistan’s retired Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood appointed as its first secretary general for a three-year term. A working committee comprising officials from member countries is also functioning. Turkiye’s ratification of the agreement has completed the accession process for all three member states, but the alliance’s institutional and operational framework remains at what Asif described as a “nascent stage”. “Initially, we need to have frequent meetings to steer what is being formulated, in a way that in the next couple of months we have everything in place so that we can move forward,” the defence minister said. The alliance has yet to publicly define its doctrine, the composition of forces, command arrangements or procedures governing a collective military response. An emergency SPDC meeting in Riyadh on Oct 5 had called for moving towards practical implementation of collective defence commitments, including arrangements for the rapid deployment of agreed forces and capabilities, subject to national laws. Wider regional tensions The alliance’s formation also comes against the backdrop of wider regional tensions involving Iran, the United States and Israel. While the three members share an interest in strengthening regional deterrence, their differing strategic priorities make it important to define the alliance’s scope without allowing it to become an instrument for wider military confrontation. Asif declined to comment on how the alliance would respond to a direct Iranian attack on Saudi Arabia, but identified Israel as a possible threat to other countries in the region. “The possibility of some conflict, or aggression from the Israeli side exists, so we need to close our ranks, the countries of this region,” he said. Managing relations with Iran will be particularly important for Pakistan, which has sought to preserve diplomatic engagement with Tehran while deepening defence cooperation with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. A meeting in Tehran involving representatives of the three countries and Iranian officials, held on Pakistan’s initiative, reflected efforts to keep channels of communication open between the two sides. Pakistan brokered a June accord that led to a brief halt in fighting between the US and Iran and laid out a roadmap for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and negotiations on Tehran’s nuclear programme. However, the truce collapsed, with Washington and Tehran accusing each other of violating the agreement, prompting months of shuttle diplomacy led principally by Qatar and Pakistan. Asif said Pakistan had played “a very, very constructive role” between Washington and Tehran, but the outcome of ongoing mediation was “still fragile” and peace was “not yet embedded in a way people were expecting”. Recent Pakistani military deployments, including JF-17 aircraft, drones and air defence systems such as the HQ-9, were made under bilateral cooperation predating the alliance, a security source said, adding that these existing arrangements would now become part of the trilateral framework. Meanwhile, Turkiye has stressed the defensive character of the agreement and remained cautious about involvement in combat operations in Yemen.

items.title: Qatar-Émirats : le Liban au cœur de deux projets régionaux concurrents
items.description: La rivalite regionale change de visage. a mesure que l'influence iranienne recule, deux projets concurrents tentent de faconner l'avenir du Liban , de la Syrie et de l'Irak. Selon une analyse de L'Orient-Le Jour publiee le 27 novembre, la competition oppose deux visions du Moyen-Orient, toutes deux proches de Washington. La premiere, incarnee par Israel et les emirats arabes unis, mise sur l'extension des accords d'Abraham, les partenariats securitaires et les corridors commerciaux reliant l'Inde, le Moyen-Orient et l'Europe. Bahreïn, la Grece et Chypre s'inscrivent aussi dans la meme dynamique. Pour Abou Dhabi, les investissements constituent un instrument d'influence regionale. Deux axes concurrents Face a cette approche, le Qatar cultive ses liens avec la Turquie et privilegie la mediation diplomatique, sans considerer la normalisation avec Israel comme un prealable. Le 13 novembre, Doha et Ankara ont reaffirme leur soutien a la souverainete libanaise et a la reconstruction syrienne. Au Liban, la concurrence se traduit par des initiatives concretes. Le Qatar envisage de financer et d'exploiter deux nouvelles centrales electriques et soutient depuis longtemps les institutions libanaises. Les emirats, de leur cote, renouent avec Beyrouth : une importante delegation economique s'y est rendue en août pour explorer des investissements dans les infrastructures et les echanges commerciaux. Mais cette recomposition se heurte a un obstacle majeur : l'avenir de l'arsenal du Hezbollah . Les operations israeliennes et les tensions autour du desarmement compliquent toute perspective de reconstruction durable. Doha et Abou Dhabi disposent de leviers diplomatiques et economiques differents, sans pouvoir resoudre seules cette crise. Pour Beyrouth, l'enjeu consiste desormais a tirer profit du regain d'interet sans devenir le terrain d'une nouvelle confrontation d'influence. Dans la competition, Washington conserve un role determinant, tandis que l'avenir du Liban apparaît de plus en plus lie aux rapports de force qui redessinent l'ensemble du Moyen-Orient.

items.title: CAITEC Group to expand into mining sector, explore new business opportunities over the next 5 years – Chairman
items.description: CAITEC Group Chairman, Mr Tang Hong, has announced plans to expand the company’s operations into new business areas, with the mining sector identified as a key focus over the next five years. He said the company was exploring new business opportunities as part of its growth strategy, following 30 years of operations in Ghana. Speaking on the sidelines of the CAITEC Group’s 30th anniversary celebration, Mr Tang said the company remained committed to strengthening its presence in the country and building on its achievements. “I have a lot of plans for the next five years, especially regarding the businesses we are involved in. We are going to expand into different areas and introduce new business opportunities,” he said. He identified mining as one of the key sectors the company intended to explore as it pursued its expansion agenda. Mr Tang, who has spent 31 years working in Ghana, described the anniversary as a significant milestone, noting that although he arrived in the country in 1995, he established CAITEC in 1996. He said the 30 years of the company’s operations represented a major achievement and expressed confidence in its prospects, indicating that the group intended to operate in Ghana for at least another three decades. “These 30 years for CAITEC mean a lot to me. I have been working in Ghana for 31 years, and it has already been 30 years for the CAITEC Group. We plan to work for another 30 years,” he said. At 60, Mr Tang acknowledged that he might not have the same physical energy and strength in another 30 years but insisted that his passion for business and affection for Ghana remained strong. He described Ghana as a wonderful country, praising its people for their kindness and hospitality. “Ghana is a wonderful country. The people are lovely, kind and hospitable. I really love Ghana. I have made a lot of speeches about how much I love this country, and I am going to stay in Ghana for the rest of my life,” he said. He reiterated his affection for the country, saying his message to Ghanaians was simply that he loved Ghana and its people. The CAITEC chairman also shared lessons from his business journey, urging entrepreneurs to develop a genuine passion for their work, remain resilient in difficult periods and exercise patience when making business decisions. He said businesses inevitably experience fluctuations and frustrating moments, making perseverance essential to achieving long-term success. “You must have passion for your business and your life. You must love what you do and love your business,” he advised. Mr Tang cautioned entrepreneurs against giving up when confronted with challenges, stressing that perseverance through difficult circumstances was necessary for sustainable growth. He also urged business owners not to rush into decisions, explaining that taking time to understand opportunities and assess situations properly could prevent costly mistakes. According to him, timing was a critical factor in business, requiring entrepreneurs to recognise when to proceed with an opportunity and when to hold back. “When it is time to move, move. When it is time to stop, stop,” he said. Mr Tang further expressed gratitude to CAITEC’s distributors for their contributions to the company’s growth over the years. He pledged to continue supplying quality products and providing the facilities and support required to strengthen their operations and partnerships. “I promise to continue bringing in good-quality products and providing the necessary facilities and support. I will make sure that I facilitate business operations with my distributor partners and make it easier for everyone to do business with CAITEC,” he said. He said the company remained committed to creating a more supportive business environment for its distributors and ensuring that their partnership with the group continued to deliver mutual benefits. The anniversary celebration marked three decades of CAITEC’s operations in Ghana, with Mr Tang reaffirming his commitment to the country’s business environment and expressing optimism about the group’s next phase of growth.

items.title: Guinea-Bissau’s military leaders delay return to civilian rule until 2028
items.description: Guinea-Bissau’s military rulers have postponed elections scheduled for next week by two years, delaying the return to civilian rule. Transitional President Gen Horta N’Tam announced in a decree that the presidential and parliamentary elections, originally due on 6 December, would now take place on 26 November 2028. The announcement came exactly a year after the military seized power, promising to return the country to civilian rule within 12 months. In a statement, the presidency said an assessment of electoral preparations had found that there were insufficient “technical, material and financial conditions” to hold the polls as planned. It said the delay would provide more time to ensure the elections were credible, transparent and inclusive, with all candidates given equal opportunities. The presidency also reiterated its commitment to holding the country’s first-ever local government elections but gave no date for the vote. Gen N’Tam was sworn in as transitional president a day after the military overthrew President Umaro Sissoco Embaló in November 2025. The coup took place three days after general elections and a day before provisional results were due to be announced. Both Embaló and his main challenger, Fernando Dias, had claimed victory. Embaló, who has since been living in exile in Morocco, was barred from returning to Guinea-Bissau last month, despite expressing an interest in contesting the elections. Guinea-Bissau has experienced several coups and attempted coups since gaining independence from Portugal in 1974.

items.title: Malaysia charges six for drug trafficking at military base
items.description: A Malaysian court has charged six people, including three Malaysian military personnel, for trafficking drugs at an air base near the capital Kuala Lumpur, local media report. Authorities say they are working to uncover the scale of suspected years-long drug smuggling involving Malaysia’s air force. At least three tonnes of drugs are believed to have been trafficked across air bases since August 2024. The suspects charged on Fridayare among 13 who were arrested earlier this month, after authorities seized 96.64kg of methamphetamine, a highly-adictive synthetic drug, at Subang Air Base. If convicted, they could be sentenced to death or life imprisonment. The drugs, concealed in five suitcases and a box, were discovered at Subang Air Base during a routine inspection. Besides the six suspects who were charged on Friday, there are seven others – four air force personnel and three civilians – who were arrested but have not been charged. One of the suspects was an air force pilot who coordinated and transported drugs from peninsular Malaysia to Sabah, a Malaysian state on the island of Borneo, police said. This is just the tip of what authorities allege are years-long drug trafficking operations involving its air force. Authorities have identified 21 cases of drug smuggling involving air force infrastructure, dating back to August 2024, Malaysia’s interior minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told parliament on Thursday. He said the drugs, which weighed a total of three tonnes, were valued at 156 million Malaysian ringgit ($37.9m; £28.9m). “Had we not dismantled this operation, millions of people would have fallen victim,” he said according to local media. “This is not merely a serious criminal offence as it also threatens the integrity of our security and defence institutions.” Saifuddin Nasution said authorities would expand the investigation to uncover the full scale of the syndicate. While they have identified the suspected leader of the syndicate, they have not made an arrest, he said. Established in the 1980s, Subang Air Base is a military airport located near the capital Kuala Lumpur. It is often used for receiving foreign dignitaries visiting Malaysia. In 2024, it was also where more than 100 Palestinians, injured and evacuated from Israel’s war on Gaza, arrived for medical treatment.

items.title: California warns of flooding as King Tides peak over Thanksgiving
items.description: Coastal areas of California are bracing for potential flooding as king tides peak inthe state during the US Thanksgiving holiday. Water levels across the US state’s vast coastline could reach over 8ft (2.4 metres) in some areas on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the National Weather Service (NWS) – breaking records set just last month. The NWS has warned parts of California could face major coastal flooding, which is likely to be significant in low-lying areas. There have already been some reports of flooding. Meanwhile, storms are also forecast for the Pacific Northwest, including the Canadian province of British Columbia, and eastern parts of the US. Portions of a pier in northern California came crashing down into the ocean on Wednesday as high tides and strong waves battered the structure, video showed. Beachgoers have been advised to stay away from the water’s edge as large waves could suddenly form. Such waves could be damaging to piers and jetties, and could capsize small vessels, the NWS warned. Flooding has already been reported in the San Francisco Bay Area. In San Diego, a high tide of 8 ft 11in was recorded on Wednesday morning local time – potentially breaking the record for highest tide measured in the area, which was just set late last month at 7.98ft. In Los Angeles, the tide on Wednesday was thought to be as high 8.19 – the record for the city that was set only weeks ago 27 October when parts of the California coast experienced flooding. Recently set high tide records were also broken in Santa Barbara and La Jolla, according to preliminary data. King tides are the highest predicted tide of the year and are above the highest water level reached at high tide on an average day. While they typically occur once or twice a year in most coastal areas, they are happening more frequently in some as sea levels rise. These king tides are being strengthened by the strongest El Niño weather pattern on record. Storm systems are also expected to impact the US through the Thanksgiving holiday – one affecting the Pacific Northwest and another the eastern part of the country, the US National Weather Service said. On the east coast, a developing Nor’easter storm is expected to bring heavy rain, strong winds, and coastal flooding. Major impacts are expected to begin on Wednesday across the southeast, and move northward Wednesday night and on Thursday, the NWS said. “Those along the eastern seaboard can expect gusty, possibly damaging winds, heavy rain, and major coastal and marine impacts,” it added. The developing storm system could bring about one to four inches rain along America’s east coast and a peak of four to six inches in coastal North Carolina. The US department store chain Macy’s has postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York, which was due to take place on Thursday, until Saturday because of severe weather – the first time this has happened. The stormy weather on both coasts could disrupt travel for millions of people. The American Automobile Association (AAA) has predicted that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles (80km) from home for Thanksgiving between Tuesday 24 November and Monday 30 November. Officials have also issued a flood warning along Vancouver’s coastline in Canada’s most western province of British Columbia. Residents were urged to take “immediate action to protect life and property”, a weather warning from Environment and Climate Change Canada said. King tides were expected to potentially increase already high water levels there too.

items.title: Tyson Fury’s wife withdraws claim that boxer has schizophrenia
items.description: Paris Fury, the wife of British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury, has withdrawn her earlier claim that her husband was diagnosed with schizophrenia, clarifying that he has never been formally diagnosed with the condition. Paris made the clarification after an earlier version of an upcoming Netflix documentary about the boxer featured her describing him as having “mild schizophrenia”. In a statement, she said she had used the term while recalling a conversation about Tyson’s mental health struggles several years ago, but acknowledged that it was not an accurate description of his medical history. “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary,” she said. “I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.” She added that mental health was complex and that finding the right words to describe someone’s experiences was not always easy. “Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love,” she said. Paris also praised her husband for speaking openly about his struggles and thanked the public for supporting their family. Netflix confirmed that it had updated the documentary following the family’s clarification about Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis. “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch,” the streaming platform said. The earlier comments had attracted attention from the British Boxing Board of Control, which indicated that it was investigating the matter. The 38 year old boxer is scheduled to face Joshua in an all British heavyweight showdown in Cardiff on December 11, with the vacant WBA title expected to be at stake. Tyson has previously spoken publicly about his mental health struggles following his victory over Ukraine’s Wladimir Klitschko in 2015, when he became world heavyweight champion. After the victory, he took a break of nearly three years from boxing, during which he battled suicidal thoughts, drug and alcohol problems, and significant weight gain. Reflecting on that period in the documentary, Tyson said he experienced severe psychological distress. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” he said. “I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 percent thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.” He later returned to boxing and regained the world heavyweight title by defeating Deontay Wilder in February 2020. Tyson suffered the first two defeats of his professional career against Oleksandr Usyk in 2024, leaving him with 39 professional fights on his record. The post Tyson Fury’s wife withdraws claim that boxer has schizophrenia appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ecobank-JoyBusiness Financial Dialogue: Businesswomen advised to research market before exporting goods
items.description: Deputy Director at the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA), Dr Martin Akogti, has urged Ghanaian Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) to research specific markets before deciding to export their products. He said this will help them identify customers’ concerns and understand how market dynamics work in each country or market. Dr Akogti made the call on the second panel of the Ecobank-JoyBusiness Financial Dialogue Series under the theme “Investing in Impact: Empowering Women-Led Businesses to Thrive.” “One has to do research into the kind of market they are going into and the behaviour of that market, because the kind of standards required in Europe might not be the same as in America”. He pointed out for example that labeling is an important step when entering the global market. “With labelling and packaging, businesses are required to put all this in place whenever they want to go into exporting,” he said, responding to questions on how small businesses can scale up to export products to other markets across the world. “One has to observe the sector one is operating in, in order to scale and become bigger. You also have to consider external partnerships with bigger players in the space and ensure that whatever products you are churning out is up to standard,” he charged. Faith-Based Account Manager at Ecobank, Susana Ama Mbroh, highlighted the critical support the bank has been providing to businesses and invited more women-led businesses to come closer for further support. “Talking about business support for our women, this is where Ecobank comes in. For us at Ecobank, we leverage our presence in about 33 countries to support businesses and help them get partnerships in other markets. We also use Ecobank Elevate to bring women businesses onto a single market where they can share ideas and gain knowledge on their business fields.” “Take the opportunity to grow and explore Ecobank products and you will never regret it,” she noted. Entrepreneur and Head of Women’s Desk at the Association of Ghana Industries, Philomena Asante, used the occasion to call on larger corporate businesses to consider patronising the services of local small businesses in order to grow the economy together. Chief Executive of Memo Mall, Mercy Adochim, expressed confidence that Ghana is moving towards women leadership, hence women businesses can get the required support. She therefore stressed the frustration in getting competent staff to grow with as a small business, and advised that small businesses must consider smaller initiatives before venturing into big-ticket deals.

items.title: The YIMBY Movement’s Greatest Success
items.description: Berkeley, California, a quintessential university town, may well be the birthplace of anti-growth politics. In 1916, local reformers adopted the country’s first single-family zoning, prohibiting apartments in most residential neighborhoods as a way to exclude disfavored minorities. Progressives would carry on this legacy for the next century in the name of protecting residents from unwanted development. Beginning in the 1960s, housing opponents tried to block construction on environmental grounds—and eventually argued that new residents qualified as “pollution.” Permitting rates were anemic for decades, keeping the city’s population flat even while enrollment at UC Berkeley skyrocketed. Rents and home prices rose accordingly. By the mid-2010s, Berkeley ranked as one of the most expensive college towns in America. But around that time, it began to undergo a remarkable reversal, as students, staff, and young faculty at UC Berkeley came to realize that housing shortages hurt their interests and began working together to push for more inclusive policies. In 2017, they helped organize the group East Bay for Everyone, which showed up constantly to public hearings and helped elect a city council aligned with the “Yes in My Backyard” movement then emerging statewide. With the aid of new state laws loosening zoning requirements—some of which I advocated for as part of my work at YIMBY organizations—permitting of new housing surged. As of 2024, nominal rents barely exceeded 2018 levels, despite inflation. Today Berkeley represents a major success for the YIMBY movement, and it’s not the only one. Across the country, college towns have become boomtowns. As longtime strongholds of progressive politics, their evolution from NIMBY holdouts to YIMBY hotbeds serves as a testament to the left’s shift on housing. If the movement’s next decade is going to deliver on the promise of its first, my fellow housing advocates nationwide will have to replicate the methods that allowed college towns to so quickly build and become more affordable. [ Jonathan Chait: The misguided Democratic opposition to permitting reform ] One obvious lesson is that students and young academics can be persuasive advocates. These groups tend to be temporarily poor and highly social and to have flexible schedules. To put this in criminological terms, they have the motive, means, and opportunity to show up in numbers at the weekday public hearings that determine what does and doesn’t get built. As a result of such activism, once-stagnant college towns across California, including San Luis Obispo and Santa Cruz, have undergone similar transformations as Berkeley: Permitting is up, and rents are starting to stabilize or sometimes even fall. At UC San Diego, campus advocates successfully pushed for new on-campus high-rises that will house thousands of students, helping alleviate the state’s extraordinary rate of student homelessness . In many college towns across the country, off -campus housing is proliferating too: Real-estate-investment trusts, often known as REITs, have plowed billions of dollars into student housing, building roughly 35,000 beds in 2024 alone. According to an estimate from 2020 , some 12 percent of all rental units are for students. Throughout the United States, college towns have taken steps to allow for greater housing density, as Ann Arbor, Michigan, did last month . Perhaps the most extreme example of this is Austin, where the flagship campus of the University of Texas is located. After a decade of trying and failing to overhaul the city zoning code, local YIMBYs began to get their way in the late 2010s, when increasing demand for housing kicked off a construction frenzy. A local backlash grew , threatening to upend the reforms that were turning Greater Austin into America’s fastest-growing metropolis. But YIMBYs were able to preserve their progress thanks in large part to one key group. “When students started to show up to Austin city-council meetings and endorse candidates based on their housing policies, and generally make it clear they want to be viewed as true constituents, it was a game changer,” Felicity Maxwell, a board member of a local pro-housing organization , told me. In 2023, with strong support from local students, lawmakers in Austin were able to sustain the city’s home-building surge by ending both single-family zoning and minimum off-street-parking requirements. The city has been building so much housing that rents are down , even as migration continues to soar. Students and junior academics cannot change decades-old urban-planning habits on their own. Senior faculty have also been instrumental in dislodging a kind of progressivism that treats all development as predatory. Well - respected professors have repeatedly called attention to the need for more housing, drawing on a growing scholarly consensus on the issue. Leaders in more and more college towns have come to see exclusionary housing as incompatible with liberal politics. “I was troubled by the tensions between Ithaca being a progressive, welcoming community that was also staggeringly unaffordable,” Robert Cantelmo, the pro-growth mayor of Ithaca, New York, told me. Cantelmo is a product of Cornell University, where he received a master’s degree and later helped lead a research center. During his tenure, Ithaca has had more active cranes than many far larger American cities. A similar story has played out in Cambridge, Massachusetts. In 2022, a recent MIT grad named Burhan Azeem mobilized students at his alma mater, who in turn helped him become the youngest councilor in the history of the city. Azeem became vice mayor earlier this year and has led a successful campaign to legalize Paris-scale density citywide. [ Read: A perfectly crude way to solve America’s housing shortage ] “Cambridge is one of the youngest towns in Massachusetts, and not just because of undergraduates,” Azeem told me. “A lot of people stay here after graduation, or stay on for years in graduate school, and their big question is, Will I ever be able to buy a home here? That makes for a natural pro-housing constituency.” In some places, however, college communities have limited political influence. At Stanford University, 98 percent of undergraduates live on campus, which is just outside Palo Alto’s municipal limits, leaving them effectively iced out from politics in that city. UC Santa Barbara is located in a county of nearly 500,000 residents, which even the most organized students would struggle to sway. In other college towns, such as Gainesville, Florida, intransigent homeowners and state governments have thwarted reform. Moreover, there are reasons to think that the college-town boom may be short-lived. University enrollment is headed for a death spiral , and dozens of colleges are closing each year. Although flagship universities and elite schools probably won’t close anytime soon, the student body at many institutions will likely shrink. But even if college towns do begin to stagnate, their runaway growth over the past decade has provided a model that YIMBYs can reproduce nationally. Housing advocates have plenty more work to do in California, where much of my advocacy has been focused. Despite its fast-growing college towns, statewide permitting is flat and housing costs are rising. In too many cases, much-anticipated reforms have failed to produce much housing. But college towns have demonstrated that transforming a community requires only a small group of highly motivated people. In California and elsewhere, such groups have made the Sisyphean task of advocacy fun , hosting happy hours , run clubs , neighborhood meetups , and workshops . “It’s really easy to point to all the abstract changes that YIMBY reforms can make at some vague point in the future,” Katie Caceres, the organizing director for the Student Homes Coalition , told me. “But real friendships are what distinguish the most successful campus groups I’ve worked with.” To ensure that college towns are a prologue to a bigger housing revolution, rather than a curious exception, YIMBYs will have to follow the example these communities set by showing up to hearings, supporting candidates, organizing lobby days, suing cities, and running for office. These steps can sometimes feel fruitless in the moment, but they’re the same ones that NIMBYs took in the 1960s and ’70s to keep Berkeley so exclusive and small. These strategies worked then to suppress growth, they worked over the past decade to restart it, and they will work now to extend it across the country.

items.title: Gift Guide for the AI Apocalypse
items.description: A cataclysm that destroys all human life is bad for many reasons, among them the resulting uselessness of a gift guide. Setting aside an extinction scenario , the more interesting—and more likely—outcome of an AI apocalypse is one in which ordinary life continues, but changed. This is closer to the biblical sense of the term apocalypse , which means a pulling back of the curtain on a divine truth. And of all the ways to prepare for an apocalypse brought about by artificial intelligence, surely the most American would be to go shopping. Before we start, here are the rules of this AI-apocalypse shopping spree. First, the calamitous scenarios (and the giftable baubles!) must be specifically connected to artificial intelligence. A backup generator and a supply of nonperishable foods would be useful in all sorts of situations: natural disasters, conventional warfare, climatological stress, terrorism. But owning them makes you a prepper of a more generic stripe. You can find lots of gift guides of those sorts in other types of publications. Godspeed. Second, the gifts need not attempt to prevent an apocalyptic outcome from arising—as if that would even be possible—nor solve a calamity once it does. The wares we seek will not avert AI ruination, but they should help curtail its impacts in a meaningful way. Perhaps more important, pondering the gift ought to help elucidate the threat itself—and reframe our understanding of what counts as an AI calamity in the first place. [ Read: Prepare for the AI apocalypse like you’d prepare for a snowstorm ] And finally, a good AI-apocalypse gift ought to be handy now, in advance of civilization-scale doomsday. The forces that might lead to bad outcomes live in the present as much as the future. Gifts for the Loss of Shared Reality The internet has undermined truth for decades now. Blogs and social-media platforms offered an alternative to the gatekeeping of traditional media. They democratized expression but also fragmented communities. Eventually, everyone’s ability to say anything all the time helped erode the institutional authority of science and the government. Accuracy became less important than engagement. These incentives industrialized misinformation, making fabrication profitable. Personalized feeds mated to algorithmic recommendations accelerated the culture of conspiracy theories. AI threatens to eradicate the fragments of truth that remain. Misinformation used to spread by accident, simply because billions of people could say anything online. Then disinformation duped people on purpose. But AI has installed automated and personalized synthetic text, images, video, and audio absolutely everywhere. It’s overwhelming. Humankind risks suffocating in so much seemingly real but actually fake information that the distinction between the two might become erased. Reality can’t be brought back entirely, but some tools can help. The Leica M-11P is a digital camera that includes hardware-authenticated digital signatures to verify the images it creates, including a record of their provenance and changes that have been made to them. The device is somewhat bulky and extremely expensive. A related alternative: any film camera. A physical negative offers material evidence of what the camera saw. Reality Defender is a software service that uses a variety of methods to detect AI manipulation in images, audio, and video. The service is intended for corporate and industrial use at a cost of about $400 a year for 1,000 scans a month, but a free plan offers 50 image analyses each month. A print-newspaper subscription is a fixed, physical version of the daily or weekly news that allows you to hold the same information as your friends and neighbors. It also offers a record of what was reported at a given time, unperturbed by questionable summaries, screenshots, or social-media posts. Gifts for the Collapse of Expertise Artificial intelligence offers an effective solution to almost any intellectual or practical problem. It can compose an email, write a job application, tell you what to eat for dinner, build a stock portfolio, offer instructions for servicing a septic tank. Or, better put, AI can appear to offer such solutions, cheaply and instantaneously. As more people and organizations take AI outputs as presumed expertise, the people who possess actual expertise in any subject could become displaced. People may stop learning how to do things for themselves—or they may come to trust the confidence of a machine, delivered effortlessly, more than they trust other people. Unlike reality, expertise really is something you can purchase, by hiring people with knowledge, experience, and credentials to carry out tasks or offer advice. This might be a graphic designer, a structural engineer, a turf-lawn-management expert, an accountant, or a tutor in a specialized subject. Your situation, and that of the individual who might receive your gift, will be particular. The trick, of course, is finding an actual expert amid the din of faux competence. If you can, recommend people you know or have worked with personally, but if you can’t, Bark offers a directory of professionals in many domains. Wikipedia isn’t a perfect host of reliable expertise, but it’s human-made and better than many alternatives. Kiwix offers an offline version of the complete English Wikipedia—along with emergency planning, repair guides, medical references, and other resources. It’s $350 as a hardware device or $35 for the data alone. The offline version is meant to defend against infrastructural collapse, but your gift recipient could use it just to access knowledge in a deliberate, internet-disconnected way. Your local library also offers an easy way to find expertise offline. Many local libraries also give you the ability to borrow ebooks, audiobooks, and magazines via the Libby app. Libraries are generally free for residents of the municipality they serve, but you need a library card to use them—and getting one typically requires an in-person visit. Overcoming that hurdle might be harder than people think. The gift, then: Take someone to lunch and then the library to get them signed up. Illustration by Vincent Kilbride Gifts for the Decline of Relationships Lunch or dinner is great for people you already know. What about people you don’t? In 2000, the political scientist Robert Putnam published Bowling Alone , the original screed against American solitude. The title refers to bowling leagues, which were once popular sources of community but fell out of favor. Putnam’s book has been enormously influential, but many readers treat bowling leagues as a metaphor rather than a concrete activity people can and do participate in. You can still go bowling! The United States Bowling Congress can help you find local leagues , memberships in which can cost as little as $10 a week . You don’t need a bowling ball to start, but affordable sets of ball, bag, and shoes make for something you can wrap. It is curious that human relationships have become so challenging to steward, given that technology allows us to connect with one another constantly and for free. Perhaps writing letters, making long-distance phone calls, and paying people a visit in person offered greater connectivity because they demanded a break from ordinary life. Some defamiliarization might help human connections thrive. You could, I suppose, give someone a stationery set and invite them to write letters again. But that feels retrograde. Instead, consider one of the oddball examples of telepresence that have been commercialized. The Friendship Lamp , for example, comes in a set of two glowing objects, one for you and one for someone else. When one of you touches the device, the other one lights up too. Bond Touch offers a similar idea in bracelet and necklace form. Gifts for Cultural Stagnation Being an artist of any kind has always been difficult, but generative AI could erode the market for human cultural production so much that such work becomes commercially unviable. When partnered with a consolidated industry for distribution, AI could even become the dominant source of what is currently known as human expression. And if AI were to replace a sufficient quantity of original human works, culture would enter a kind of death spiral, in which no new art can arise except as rehashings of what came before. The best way to combat the automation of human culture is to support culture itself. This can’t be done just once, but must happen over and over again, as a practice. A season pass to your local symphony, theater, or ballet offers one way to help someone develop such a relationship. So does buying real art from real artists—galleries in your area are bound to offer affordable drawings, prints, paintings, and plastic arts that can help start a collection. Many bookstores feature works by local writers too. Culture would be better if more people produced it in addition to consuming it. Digital life confused that process. It appeared to democratize creation, giving everyone the tools to make music, writing, art, and moving images—and then distribute their wares globally. Online platforms also distorted culture into a thing primarily meant to produce attention and monetization. Nothing was really ever stopping you from learning to produce (and then improve) your own cultural work, whether music, writing, painting, ceramics, or whatever else that might strike you. Buy a violin or an easel (or anything of the sort that seems right for your gift recipient), along with a local class to get them started. Illustration by Vincent Kilbride Gifts for the Unabiding Din of Machines AI chats you up constantly now. Word processors, apps, even Google searches now typically initiate a conversation with an AI agent, whether you asked for one or not. Digital-detox gifts offer one way to quell the noise: for example, a redesigned but old-school media device such as the Fosi Audio compact-disc player , a deliberately limited digital device such as the Light Phone , or the Brick smartphone lock. But those options are defensive. By contrast, an array of objects that offer simple, quiet, and unmediated attention remains available. A nice mechanical wristwatch—or even a simple, cheap Casio—can do it. So can a good kitchen tool, such as an ice-cream scoop or a potato ricer. A delightful notebook and writing implement are always good for some quiet, as is a print book of almost any type. Gifts for the Digital Panopticon Years ago, information such as your home address and voting history might have been available in public records, but they were obfuscated by the need to access them in person. Online services ended that. And then, Big Tech started collecting and sharing information about you, with or without your permission. AI extends that tendency by improving machines’ abilities to infer knowledge about individuals—including intimate facts—from the ever-enlarging supply of data (including apparently innocuous data) constantly collected by apps, services, sensors, facial-recognition cameras, transaction records, and more. The ability to carry out one’s life in modest obscurity had already become difficult. AI could do away with it entirely. [ Read: Read this website while you still can ] You can buy tools that can, to some extent, defend against digital surveillance: a Faraday bag can block incoming and outgoing signals when you put your smartphone inside it; a service such as DeleteMe finds and removes information about you online; and adversarial apparel can stymie computer-vision surveillance . But you can also reduce your digital footprint in simpler ways. An envelope of cash allows your gift recipient to spend money without creating a transaction record for data-broker discovery. A nice paper planner allows you to keep a calendar without sharing your deeds with Google. Gmail can scan all of your emails for advertising targeting, something a private email account on a service such as Proton Mail or Apple iCloud+ does not. A subscription, along with a custom domain name, would make for a privacy-forward gift. Gifts for the Swamp of Sycophancy Large language models tend to affirm what a user provides as input—“I agree”—even if that entails validating flawed views or circumventing accurate responses. Over time, AI models’ designers may reduce this sycophancy effect, but they will have to overcome a strong incentive not to do so: an agreeable and even obsequious AI creates greater engagement, use, and thereby value for the AI companies. Should AI’s tendency to grovel increase while human reliance on it also expands, then a plurality of people may come to expect and acclimate to sycophancy in every nook and cranny of ordinary life. To help someone wade out of the swamp, a gift needs to offer psychological and social effects rather than utility or even delight. A demanding book of puzzles is an option, such as Cain’s Jawbone (a legendary 1934 literary puzzle) and The New York Times Seriously Hard Crossword Puzzles . A difficult or complex board game ( Car Wars , perhaps, or High Frontier 4 All ) or video game (such as Dark Souls ) could fit the bill too. Physical activity also has a role to play: A couple of trips to an indoor-climbing wall or a few consultations with a personal trainer might be enough to reveal that the world was not built for you alone. Gifts for Trust’s Twilight The loss of shared reality, fueled by the swamp of sycophancy, could cause members of the public to withdraw into their own addled, private realities. Just as likely, it could ignite paranoia. Every email, text message, phone call, viral video, and internet post that seems authentic might also be fake. AI impersonation, already enormously convincing, is poised to improve, and tools to detect evidence of AI intervention in text and audiovisual material remain dubious. Once every shard of apparently earnest or human-created content raises suspicion, almost nothing will seem trustworthy. When trust itself cannot be assumed, perhaps ever, an almost delusional suspicion may become the default mode of interaction. Some companies are trying to solve the trust problems that computers create with … more computers. Hardware-security keys such as YubiKey offer better protection against phishing and hacking attacks than password managers or two-factor authentication. And Vicem, designed to avert telephone scams, offers an AI phone monitor . Other, simpler tools also exist. You can still get a landline number that you don’t share publicly—or a supposedly private virtual number from a service such as GetUnlisted . A more baroque (and affected) solution from the past: a personalized wax seal , along with stationery on which to apply it. Illustration by Vincent Kilbride Gifts for the End of Serendipity Optimization and efficiency, once values of business alone, have leaked into ordinary life. The practice of living one’s life—dating, parenting, dining out, working, even seeking leisure—has turned into accomplishing tasks along the way to supposedly even better tasks. In the end, human life may turn away from any encounter whose outcome is not predictable, even known in advance. Contingency, accident, and improvisation could disappear as people eschew those putatively useless disomforts—and then forget about them entirely. In a way, a good gift of any kind—AI-aware or not—counts as a gift of serendipity. Something given as a true surprise, and perhaps even absent of need, offers a door to an unexpected act. I can’t tell you what might count as such a gift for the individuals on your list; consider it a gift of judgment to ponder the matter. One idea: a paper map or atlas, the kind that can live in a car’s seat-back pocket. It might inspire someone to use a city absent computer guidance. Serendipity may be on the decline, but many of the sources that once delivered it remain available, if in fragile forms. A monthly print-magazine subscription ( such as this one ) puts a package of surprising stories in the mailbox on the regular. A short-wave radio , or an HDTV antenna and HDHomeRun device, delivers whatever is being broadcast right now to your home. A gift certificate to a local shop with no online ordering, or to a local restaurant that does not offer delivery, can ignite the delight of browsing again. A n apocalypse feels like something you can do nothing about beyond panicking or hunkering down, as if awaiting a meteor’s collision with Earth. [ Read: What if the apocalypse is already here? ] But “apocalypse” may not be the right way to understand the distinctive challenges that artificial intelligence presents to human life. The temptation to catastrophize—an urge the internet rewarded long before AI—can obscure the ways that ordinary life can steer nimbly around cataclysm simply by each of us making modest choices where alternatives are available. When carried out in the best spirit, gifts allow recipients and givers alike to see the world, and their place in it, in a marginally different light. This makes the holidays an ideal time to imagine and then embrace slightly different ways of living. None of artificial intelligence’s apocalypses, at least the ones humankind might survive, represents wholly new circumstances that AI invented. Instead, artificial intelligence wore deeper ruts into prior habits. One such rut is the discourse surrounding artificial intelligence: Either the world will be saved by AI, or else AI will ruin it. You and I and all of the people on your holiday gift list get cast as passengers, careening toward deliverance or doom. The reality will probably be more banal. Most of AI’s threats are not existential, and likewise many of the defenses against those threats will not defeat the technology. The survival equipment suitable to fortify against that erosion will be correspondingly ordinary. A notebook preserves the capacity to write. A violin hands down the experience of making music. A dinner out demands face-to-face interactions with friends. A telephone whose number only a few people know rings with delight rather than foreboding. A paper map requires interpretation; a library invites perusal; a bowling lane can facilitate new conversation. The world is not ending.

items.title: PM calls for effective guidance, simplified procedures for SMEs seeking financial support
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday called for better guidance for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) seeking financing from banks, enabling access to loans through simplified procedures. Presiding over a meeting on facilitating access to credit for SMEs, the premier termed these enterprises the “backbone” of the country’s economy. “Facilitating them will boost economic activity, employment and business opportunities,” the prime minister said. The prime minister directed the provision of effective guidance and support to SMEs to improve their access to financial resources, prepare business documentation and benefit from opportunities in the export sector. He called for further simplification of the procedures for SMEs to obtain loans. “SMEs with export data available through the Pakistan Single Window, or those integrated into supply chains through Exim Insurance and digital invoicing, should be considered for loans against these records as collateral,” the prime minister said. He also directed that banks consider SMEs’ cash flows as an alternative measure of collateral for lending. PM Shehbaz called for a review of prudential regulations governing bank lending to SMEs. He further directed that banks be granted access to relevant data held by government institutions to expedite the lending process for these companies. To facilitate SMEs, banks should not only provide loans but also assist them in issuing letters of credit (LCs) and providing bank guarantees, the PM said at the meeting. He added that banks achieving their prescribed SME lending targets would be encouraged. The meeting was informed that banks were taking steps to strengthen their institutional capacity to accelerate lending to SMEs. The banks expressed their commitment to achieving a target of providing Rs2 trillion in loans to SMEs by June 2028 and increasing the number of SME borrowers to 775,000. The target includes the disbursement of Rs886bn in new loans and the provision of financial facilities to 449,000 new borrowers. Federal ministers Rana Tanveer Hussain, Ahsan Khan Cheema and Riaz Hussain Pirzada; PM’s Adviser Haroon Akhtar; Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kiyani; State Bank Governor Jameel Ahmad; chief executive officers of the National Bank of Pakistan, Bank Alfalah and the Bank of Punjab; and senior officials of relevant institutions attended the meeting. Last week, PM Shehbaz approved the establishment of facilitation centres for SMEs at the district level, with pilot projects in Lahore, Peshawar, Karachi and Quetta. In October, he directed authorities to increase financing for SMEs from Rs1.1tr to Rs2.2tr by 2028, citing their potential to drive economic growth and create business opportunities across the country.

items.title: SOGUIPAH : les financements de l’usine de 6 tonnes/heure bouclés, la relance se précise (Julien Dramou, DG)
items.description: Au sortir d’une session extraordinaire de son conseil d’administration, tenue mercredi dernier dans un complexe hôtelier de Conakry et qui a duré plusieurs heures, Julien Dramou, directeur général de la Société guinéenne de palmier à huile et d’hévéa (SOGUIPAH SA), affiche son optimisme. Les administrateurs ont notamment approuvé plusieurs projets de financement, le plan de sortie de crise et examiné les états financiers des exercices 2023, 2024 et 2025. La finalisation de l’usine de transformation de 6 tonnes/heure figure parmi les principaux chantiers annoncés. Dans cet entretien, Julien Dramou revient sur les décisions prises par le conseil d’administration, les grands axes du processus de relance et les perspectives de redressement durable de la société.… Journaliste : la SOGUIPAH a tenu une session extraordinaire de son conseil d’administration. À l’issue de cette rencontre, que peut-on retenir ? Julien Dramou : Je sors de cette session du conseil d’administration avec un sentiment de satisfaction, notamment au regard du travail abattu par les administrateurs, sous la conduite de Madame la présidente du conseil. Les administrateurs ont consacré toute une journée, de 10 h à 20 h, à examiner minutieusement les projets de décisions soumis à leur appréciation par la direction générale. Ils ont approuvé la majorité de ces projets, notamment ceux relatifs aux financements proposés, aux documents stratégiques, dont le plan de sortie de crise et d’urgence, ainsi qu’à l’examen des états financiers des trois derniers exercices, à savoir 2023, 2024 et 2025. Les recommandations formulées seront prises en compte par la direction générale. Nous allons très rapidement commencer à mettre en œuvre le plan de sortie de crise, qui comporte de nombreuses actions. Celles-ci seront rendues publiques dans les meilleurs délais, afin que les populations sachent qu’il existe certes des difficultés à la SOGUIPAH, mais également des mesures correctives et des actions de remédiation prévues pour les mois et les années à venir. L’objectif est de sortir durablement de cette crise, afin que la société ne retombe plus dans les mêmes difficultés, mais poursuive plutôt sa marche vers la prospérité. Quels sont les principaux chantiers prévus pour relancer la SOGUIPAH ? Les principaux chantiers de relance reposent sur plusieurs leviers qui ont été identifiés. Il s’agit notamment de la finalisation de l’usine de 6 tonnes par heure, actuellement en construction. Le financement de ce projet faisait défaut, mais nous avons aujourd’hui réussi à boucler les financements nécessaires, et le conseil d’administration vient de les approuver. Dans les prochains jours, les conventions devraient être signées. Les médias seront invités à prendre part à la cérémonie de signature avec les partenaires qui ont bien voulu nous accompagner dans cette démarche. Quel message souhaitez-vous adresser aux travailleurs et aux partenaires de la SOGUIPAH à l’issue de ce conseil d’administration ? Aujourd’hui, il faut privilégier la sensibilisation et appeler chacun à la retenue et au calme. Certes, les difficultés sont nombreuses et les défis ont été importants, mais ils pourront être relevés grâce à l’appui et à l’engagement de tous les acteurs et de toutes les parties prenantes. Vous savez qu’une mission d’information parlementaire s’est rendue à la SOGUIPAH il y a quelques jours. Cette mission formulera certainement des recommandations qui contribueront à conforter le gouvernement dans sa volonté d’accompagner la SOGUIPAH dans son processus de relance. Au-delà de cette mission parlementaire, toutes les actions que le conseil d’administration vient de valider sont de nature à favoriser une relance durable de la société. Pour nous, aujourd’hui, nous sommes sur la bonne pente. Si nous devions qualifier cette dynamique, nous dirions que la SOGUIPAH se remet sur la rampe de lancement. Propos recueillis par Ousmane CAMARA L’article SOGUIPAH : les financements de l’usine de 6 tonnes/heure bouclés, la relance se précise (Julien Dramou, DG) est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.description: El PP ha presentado este viernes ante la Junta Electoral Central un escrito para denunciar las “graves incidencias en la entrega de la documentación del voto por correo y en el reparto de la propaganda electoral”. Según asegura el partido en un comunicado, ha recibido “numerosas quejas de electores que, habiendo solicitado el voto por correo, no han recibido la documentación o la han recibido con retraso”. Mientras, el presidente del Gobierno y candidato socialista a la reelección en las elecciones generales del 29-N, Pedro Sánchez, ha llamado a “optimizar el voto” el próximo domingo. Por su parte, el líder del Partido Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ha reiterado la expresión “calladita” que lanzó a la candidata de Frente Amplio, Ada Colau, durante el debate a cuatro celebrado anoche, al tiempo que ha intentado restarle importancia agregando: “Han estado calladitos y calladitas durante estos siete largos años”. Sánchez ha asegurado que cuenta con datos para creer que el PSOE puede ganar las elecciones y formar una mayoría parlamentaria para revalidar un Gobierno progresista. La campaña electoral concluye hoy, con Sánchez y Colau en Madrid; Feijóo, en Sevilla y Santiago Abascal (Vox) en Valencia. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Législatives et municipales au Cameroun : 15 partis politiques ambitionnent de conquérir 304 sièges dans le Mfoundi
items.description: © DR Ils ont manifesté leur intérêt de participer aux élections législatives et municipales en déposant des listes de candidature auprès d’Elections Cameroon. Le RDPC et le MRC visent la totalité des sièges. Les élections du 07 février 2027 s’annoncent disputées dans le département du Mfoundi qui couvre la ville de Yaoundé. 15 partis politiques attendent la validation des listes de candidature qu’ils ont déposées auprès d’Elections Cameroon. D’après les données du préfet du département du Mfoundi, Emmanuel Mariel Djikdent, quatre partis politiques ont déposé des dossiers pour les élections législatives dans le Mfoundi. Le RDPC, le MRC, le PCRN et le parti Jouvence ont chacun l’intention de remporter les sept sièges de députés attribués au département du Mfoundi. Pour les élections municipales, 14 partis politiques ont introduit des dossiers de candidatures pour participer au scrutin dans les sept communes du département du Mfoundi. Le Mouvement pour la Renaissance du Cameroun et le Rassemblement démocratique du peuple camerounais s’engagent dans la compétition dans l’ensemble des communes pour un total de 297 sièges à pourvoir tandis que le PCRN ciblent quatre communes. Dans le détail, les autres partis politiques ont fait une sélection des communes dans lesquelles ils peuvent peser dans les urnes. A Yaoundé 1 er où 41 sièges de conseillers municipaux sont à pourvoir au terme des élections, le FDC et l’UNDP ont aussi l’ambition de convaincre les électeurs comme le MRC et le RDPC. A Yaoundé 2, cinq partis ont déposé les dossiers en plus des deux qui sont partout, le PSG, l’UMS et le FC sont attente de confirmation. A Yaoundé 3, le MRC, le RDPC et le PSG pourront croiser le fer pour les 41 sièges à pourvoir. A Yaoundé 4, le plus grand réservoir de sièges de conseillers municipaux du Mfoundi (61 au total), quatre partis politiques sont intéressés : le RDPC, le MRC, le PCRN et le SDF. Comme Yaoundé 3, la commune de Yaoundé 5 est la moins convoitée. Trois partis politiques se proposent de conquérir 41 sièges : le RDPC, le MRC, le PCRN. Yaoundé 6 est la plus convoitée des communes du Mfoundi. Neuf partis politiques ont l’intention de batailler pour remporter les 41 sièges : le RDPC, le MRC, le FDC, l’UPC, le SDF, le PCRN, le PRP, le PADDEC et le MP3. A Yaoundé 7, six partis politiques ont l’ambition de conquérir les 31 sièges disponibles : le RDPC, le MRC, le PDC, le PURC, le PCRN, le FDC. Dans quelques jours, la liste des partis politiques retenus et la liste des partis politiques rejetés seront rendues publiques et la carte des élections législatives et municipales sera fixée. Cet article Législatives et municipales au Cameroun : 15 partis politiques ambitionnent de conquérir 304 sièges dans le Mfoundi est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Culture : Med C lance son album « La Relève » ce vendredi au Palais du Peuple
items.description: Le compte à rebours est lancé pour Med C. L’artiste guinéen s’apprête à dévoiler officiellement, ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026, son nouvel album baptisé « La Relève ». Avant ce rendez-vous, il a présenté les contours de ce projet lors d’une conférence de presse organisée à Conakry. Un album à travers lequel il revendique son héritage musical, rend hommage à ceux qui ont accompagné son parcours et affiche l’ambition de s’imposer bien au-delà de Kaloum. Le lancement sera marqué par un concert au Palais du Peuple. La rencontre avec la presse a réuni plusieurs acteurs du monde culturel, parmi lesquels Chamack et Koury Simplé. L’artiste, son équipe de production ainsi que son père, Bouba Mengué, ont notamment expliqué les motivations ayant conduit à la réalisation de cet album et les attentes liées à son lancement. Pour Med C, le titre de l’album traduit avant tout une continuité. Fils de Bouba Mengué, membre des Espoirs de Coronthie, l’artiste estime porter la responsabilité de prolonger une histoire musicale qui dépasse sa seule génération. Il se présente comme le seul fils des Espoirs de Coronthie à avoir choisi de poursuivre cette voie et considère son parcours comme une manière de représenter plusieurs formations emblématiques de Kaloum. «Aujourd’hui, tout le monde parle de Med C. Med C, je suis le fils d’un artiste et du groupe d’artistes qui sont les Espoirs de Coronthie, les Ambassadeurs de Boulbinet, les Étoiles de Boulbinet et les Messagers. Donc, des Degg J Force 3. Med C est le seul artiste, le seul fils des Espoirs de Coronthie qui représente tous ces groupes. C’est pourquoi on parle de La Relève », a-t-il expliqué. Mais l’album ne se limite pas à cette dimension familiale. Med C annonce également un projet consacré à des sujets universels, notamment l’amour, la vie, l’aventure et la mort. « Dans cet album, on va parler de l’amour, de la vie, de l’aventure et de la mort parce qu’aujourd’hui on est là, demain on va être où ? Je ne sais pas », a-t-il confié. Pour son manager principal, Poutine Boiro, « La Relève » doit également servir de passerelle entre les générations. Il présente Med C comme un ambassadeur culturel de Kaloum, appelé à faire rayonner cet héritage au-delà de la commune. Sur le plan musical, l’album compte 16 titres, dont 13 chansons et trois bonus. Parmi les 13 morceaux, trois collaborations sont annoncées, notamment avec l’artiste international Mohamed Diaby et Bouba Mengué, père de Med C. Le manager promet un projet porté par une diversité de sonorités et de messages. La préparation de l’album s’est étalée sur plus d’une année. Mohamed Camara, responsable de MCiss Prod, indique que la signature avec Med C remonte à mai 2025 et que le travail sur le projet a débuté il y a environ un an. Ancien professionnel des médias, il explique avoir choisi de ne pas communiquer publiquement au moment de la signature. « On signe un talent, ce n’est pas une actualité. Quelqu’un qui signe un talent, la personne vient en aide, mais quand c’est une célébrité qui signe, ça devient une actualité. Donc je ne veux pas faire du bruit. C’est pour cela que je n’ai pas fait de communication dessus », a-t-il expliqué. Le producteur assure par ailleurs avoir engagé personnellement des moyens pour accompagner l’artiste, malgré des ressources limitées, tout en reconnaissant le travail effectué auparavant par l’équipe qui avait contribué à installer Med C dans le paysage musical. « Je me suis investi corps et âme pour satisfaire les besoins de l’artiste, pas parce que je suis riche. Bon, les amis de la presse ici le savent, ce sont les petits salaires qu’on combine pour faire ce projet », a-t-il révélé. La production de l’album a nécessité plusieurs déplacements. Des séances d’enregistrement ont notamment été réalisées en Guinée, au Mali, en Côte d’Ivoire et en France. Au-delà de la sortie de l’album, le concert prévu au Palais du Peuple constitue l’un des principaux enjeux pour l’équipe de Med C. Mory Traoré, chef de projet, insiste sur le caractère collectif de cette aventure et sur le rôle de toutes les personnes qui ont contribué à construire le parcours de l’artiste. Il reconnaît notamment que l’équipe actuelle a repris un travail déjà engagé et tient à rendre hommage à ceux qui l’ont précédée. « Il faut avoir le courage de le dire : merci à ceux qui ont pris Med C jusque-là où nous, on l’a pris. Ils ont fait un boulot qui nous a facilité la tâche. Donc, on ne peut pas être là aujourd’hui et leur voler cette vedette. Il faut les remercier même s’ils ne sont pas tous là aujourd’hui », a-t-il déclaré. Mory Traoré salue également l’implication de MCiss Prod et des différentes équipes mobilisées autour de l’artiste. Malgré la forte concurrence entre les sorties musicales, il estime que Med C a réussi à occuper une place dans l’actualité culturelle. À quelques heures du concert, il affiche sa confiance dans le dispositif mis en place et dans la capacité de l’équipe à mobiliser le public. « Demain, on ne dormira que quand l’administration du Palais nous dira : “Arrêtez maintenant.” Et on a confiance en nos stratégies, on a confiance en l’artiste, on a confiance en l’équipe de pilotage, on a confiance à toutes les parties prenantes », a-t-il assuré. Poutine Boiro indique, pour sa part, que les ventes de tickets se situent déjà entre 80 et 90 % de l’objectif fixé. L’enjeu, selon le manager, dépasse toutefois la seule réussite du concert. Il souhaite que « La Relève » permette à Med C de sortir du seul cadre de Kaloum, de toucher le public dans les autres régions de Guinée et, à terme, de franchir les frontières nationales. La conférence de presse a également été marquée par l’intervention de Bouba Mengué, père de Med C et membre des Espoirs de Coronthie. Il est revenu sur son opposition initiale à voir son fils se lancer dans la musique. Il a notamment profité de cette occasion pour demander pardon aux premières personnes qui avaient accompagné la carrière de son fils, dont Mohamed Camara. « Toute la Guinée sait que son père ne voulait pas qu’il chante. Donc, aux premières personnes qui ont insisté là, demandez-leur pardon. Tu peux engendrer un enfant et ne pas bénéficier de ses retombées. C’est la situation entre eux et Med C. Donc, je leur demande pardon et aussi, je les remercie », a-t-il déclaré. Il a également reconnu l’engagement du producteur dans le financement et l’accompagnement du projet, estimant que cet investissement devait être salué. Mais au-delà de l’héritage familial, Bouba Mengué encourage son fils à construire son propre chemin artistique. « C’est Med C qui a créé sa propre histoire. L’homme crée sa propre histoire et l’histoire parle de lui. Son père a créé son histoire et l’enfant fera de même », a-t-il affirmé. Il a également évoqué les encouragements reçus au sein des Espoirs de Coronthie. Il cite notamment Aly 100 Song, qui l’avait encouragé à laisser le jeune artiste suivre sa propre voie, avec l’espoir qu’il puisse atteindre des horizons que ses aînés n’avaient pas connus. Avec «La Relève », Med C veut ainsi conjuguer héritage et identité personnelle. L’artiste entend assumer l’histoire musicale dont il est issu tout en inscrivant son propre nom dans la nouvelle génération. À la veille du concert, il s’est directement adressé à son public, qu’il appelle ses « révolutionnaires », pour l’inviter à se mobiliser. «J’invite tous les fans, tous mes révolutionnaires demain au Palais du Peuple pour venir fêter le baptême de leur fils Med C, Mohamed Camara », a-t-il lancé. Le rendez-vous est donc fixé à ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026 au Palais du Peuple pour le lancement de « La Relève », un album de 16 titres que Med C et son équipe présentent comme une nouvelle étape de son parcours, entre héritage musical, affirmation artistique et volonté de conquérir un public au-delà de Kaloum. items.title: Full list: Italy unveils 14 African countries eligible for work visas
items.description: Italy has listed 14 African countries whose citizens are eligible to apply for work visas under its 2026–2028 immigration programme, offering employment opportunities to foreign workers across several sectors of its economy. Nigeria is among the African countries on the list, alongside Ghana, Senegal, Morocco, Egypt and 10 others. The programme forms part of Italy’s broader labour migration policy, which seeks to admit foreign workers to address labour shortages and meet the country’s employment needs. Under the programme, the Italian government has reserved 25,000 work permits annually for citizens of 38 designated countries, including the 14 African nations. The African countries named are: Algeria Ivory Coast Egypt Ethiopia The Gambia Ghana Mali Morocco Mauritius Niger Nigeria Senegal Sudan Tunisia. The employment opportunities cover sectors including agriculture, forestry, fishing, food production, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail trade, hospitality, tourism, transportation, logistics, healthcare and social assistance. According to the Italian Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, the immigration programme provides for a total of 497,550 foreign workers to enter Italy between 2026 and 2028. The allocation is divided into 164,850 workers for 2026, 165,850 for 2027 and 166,850 for 2028. The figures cover seasonal and non-seasonal employment as well as self-employment. However, inclusion on the list does not automatically guarantee a work visa. Applicants must secure employment from an Italian employer, who is generally required to apply for the relevant work authorisation, known as nulla osta , before the worker proceeds with the visa application. For the 2026 allocation, applications for seasonal agricultural jobs were scheduled to open on January 12, while those for seasonal tourism jobs were scheduled for February 9. Applications for non-seasonal employment under the relevant categories were scheduled for February 16 and 18, 2026. The programme is part of Italy’s efforts to address labour shortages through regulated migration while strengthening cooperation with countries of origin. items.title: UK Reform leader vows to scrap Graduate visa route used by 20,478 Nigerians
items.description: UK Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, has vowed to scrap the United Kingdom’s Graduate visa route if his party wins power, a move that could affect thousands of Nigerians who use the scheme to remain in the country after completing their studies. Farage announced the proposal in a post on X on Thursday, arguing that the route allows foreign graduates to stay in the UK for two years after completing their degrees, competing with British workers for entry level jobs or potentially claiming asylum. Figures published by the UK Home Office on November 26 showed that 20,478 Nigerian nationals received grants under the Graduate route in the year to September 2026, making Nigerians the third largest group of beneficiaries. Indian nationals topped the list with 66,552 grants, followed by Pakistanis with 24,768. The three nationalities accounted for about 69 per cent of all grants recorded during the period. The Graduate route allows international students who have completed eligible courses at UK universities to remain in the country and work or look for employment without needing an immediate job offer or sponsorship. Reform UK’s home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf, has described the scheme as “a scam on the British people” and proposed replacing it with a 30 day period for graduates to secure a qualifying job that meets an economic value test. The party said about 800,000 Graduate visas, including those issued to dependants, had been granted since the route was introduced in July 2021. Yusuf also cited Home Office figures showing that 5,130 asylum claims were made by people who had previously held Graduate visas in the year to June 2026, twice the number recorded in the preceding year. The pledge comes as the Labour government is already preparing to reduce the standard duration of the Graduate visa from two years to 18 months from January 1, 2027. The change will not apply to graduates from institutions that meet certain compliance and labour market outcome standards. However, Reform UK has yet to clarify how its proposed abolition would affect people who already hold Graduate visas or international students currently studying in the country. The latest Home Office figures also showed a decline in the number of Nigerian students receiving sponsored study visas. Grants to Nigerian nationals fell by 34 per cent to 19,734 in the year to September 2026, representing about six per cent of the total.
