items.title: Ondo: Supreme Court affirms Arobo as APC Reps candidate for Owo/Ose
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — The Supreme Court on Friday affirmed the judgment directing the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise Mr. Abdulghani Arobo as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for the Owo/Ose Federal Constituency of Ondo State in the 2027 general elections. In a unanimous decision by a five-member panel of justices, the apex court held that evidence before it established that Arobo scored the majority of lawful votes cast at the primary election conducted by the APC. The apex court, in its lead judgment delivered by Justice Mohammed Idris Baba, said it found no reason to dislodge the concurrent decisions of both the Federal High Court and the Court of Appeal, which declared Arobo the bona fide winner of the APC House of Reps ticket. Consequently, it dismissed, as lacking in merit, two separate appeals marked SC/CV/830/2026 and SC/CV/795/2026, which were lodged by the APC and its preferred candidate for the election, Mr. Oluwatimehin Adelegbe. The appellants had sought to set aside the October 9 judgment of the Abuja Division of the Court of Appeal, which directed INEC to recognise Arobo as the authentic candidate of the APC for the election. In processes before the court, Adelegbe insisted that he won the primary election the APC conducted in the constituency on May 16 and was duly nominated as the party’s candidate for the seat. He faulted the Court of Appeal’s refusal of his application to tender evidence to prove that he won the primary and that his name was uploaded by the APC to INEC’s portal as the party’s candidate for the House of Reps election. Listed as respondents in the appeal were Arobo, the APC and INEC. According to the appellant, the appellate court, in deciding the appeal marked CA/ABJ/CV/1235/2026, wrongly affirmed an earlier verdict that Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja delivered on August 5, which recognised Arobo as the APC flag bearer. In the 18 grounds of appeal filed before the Supreme Court through his team of lawyers led by Mr. Joseph Daudu, SAN, Adelegbe contended that the judgments of the lower courts occasioned a miscarriage of justice against him. Alleging that he was denied a fair hearing, the appellant told the apex court that he was not joined as an interested party in the suit that led to his removal as the APC candidate for the election. The appellant further contended that the court’s refusal to grant a motion on notice, brought pursuant to Order 4 Rule 2 of the Court of Appeal Rules 2021, for leave to adduce fresh or additional evidence, proved fatal to his case. He identified the additional evidence sought to be tendered as statutory public documents, which included the APC’s official candidate forwarding letter dated June 26, 2026; his Form EC9 affidavit; the INEC Candidate Nomination Portal (ICNP) submission receipt dated July 11, 2026; and a certified true copy (CTC) of the official APC Election Committee result sheet, showing that he polled 13,094 votes. Adelegbe said the essence of the application was that, had Arobo joined him as a party in the suit leading to the High Court judgment, he would have provided sufficient evidence showing that he was the person declared the winner of the APC primary for the Owo/Ose Federal Constituency. On another ground of appeal, he argued that the Court of Appeal erred in law and reached a perverse decision when it affirmed the trial court’s judgment, which was delivered in total breach of Section 36(1) of the 1999 Constitution and without joining him as an indispensable and necessary party, upon the erroneous finding that no final declaration or return had been made in his favour. He said the appellate court erred in law when it held that he was bound by the trial court’s proceedings under the doctrine of “standing by” and that his interests were adequately represented and defended by the APC. It was further the appellant’s position that the doctrine of estoppel by “standing by” strictly requires clear proof that the non-party had full, actual notice of the institution and pendency of the suit, possessed a direct interest in the subject matter, and consciously made an informed election to stand by and allow others to fight his cause on his behalf. Adelegbe noted that he deposed in his uncontroverted affidavits that he was never served with any documents relating to the suit filed by Arobo, on which the trial court’s judgment was based, and hence he “had absolutely no actual or constructive knowledge of the suit until after final judgment was delivered behind his back on 5th August 2026, thereby making it legally impossible to invoke the doctrine of ‘standing by’ against him.” He added that the Court of Appeal erred in law when it held that Arobo was justified in bypassing the final appellate organ of the APC, the National Working Committee (NWC), after waiting 11 days. The appellant also faulted the appellate court for holding that Arobo’s suit at the trial court was properly commenced by originating summons under Paragraph 7(1) of the Pre-Election Practice Directions 2026, despite “grave, hostile and conflicting factual allegations raised in the suit.” He prayed the apex court to issue an order affirming his candidacy and directing INEC to recognise, publish and maintain his name, profile and nomination particulars as the duly nominated candidate of the APC for the constituency. Likewise, the APC, in its appeal, insisted that Adelegbe was validly nominated. However, the Supreme Court held that there was no merit in the appeals, which it dismissed without cost. In his reaction shortly after the judgment, Arobo, who applauded the judiciary for doing justice in the matter, urged his opponents to close ranks and support him to ensure victory for the party at the poll. items.title: La crise de la Cnam menace la continuité d’approvisionnement en médicaments
items.description: La Chambre syndicale nationale des pharmaciens grossistes-répartiteurs (CSPGR), affiliée à l’Union tunisienne de l’industrie, du commerce et de l’artisanat (Utica), alerte l’opinion publique en Tunisie, dans une déclaration publiée vendredi 27 novembre 2026, sur la persistance et l’aggravation de la crise financière de la Caisse nationale d’assurance-maladie (Cnam) qui, selon elle, «menace la continuité de l’approvisionnement en médicaments ainsi que la sécurité sanitaire nationale». Tout en exprimant «sa vive préoccupation face à l’aggravation de la crise financière découlant de l’accumulation des créances des officines privées auprès de la Cnam» , ladite Chambre estime que «cette situation engendre de graves répercussions qui menacent la stabilité du système national du médicament.» «Cette crise a eu un impact direct sur les entreprises de distribution pharmaceutique en gros, se traduisant par des difficultés à recouvrer leurs créances auprès des officines, une détérioration de leur trésorerie et un épuisement de leurs capacités de financement. Cette situation entrave désormais leur capacité à honorer leurs engagements envers leurs fournisseurs, au premier rang desquels figurent la Pharmacie Centrale de Tunisie et les laboratoires pharmaceutiques» , souligne la CSPGR. «Malgré les efforts déployés pour garantir la continuité de l’approvisionnement et de la distribution des médicaments sur l’ensemble du territoire national, les capacités financières des entreprises de distribution sont au bord de l’épuisement ; elles ne sont plus en mesure de continuer à financer indirectement le système d’assurance-maladie en puisant dans leurs propres ressources» , avertit-elle. Tout en réitérant sa totale solidarité avec les pharmaciens titulaires d'officines privées, la Chambre syndicale «appelle les autorités publiques à intervenir d’urgence pour trouver une solution radicale à cette crise et garantir le règlement des arriérés dans des délais clairement définis» , car, avertit-elle, «la poursuite de cette situation risque d’aggraver la pénurie de médicaments et de perturber les circuits d’approvisionnement, ce qui pourrait conduire à une paralysie progressive du système de distribution des médicaments.» Tout en réaffirmant le droit du citoyen tunisien à l’accès aux médicaments, lequel «ne saurait être pris en otage par les déséquilibres financiers du système d’assurance-maladie», la Chambre syndicale «exhorte les autorités compétentes à prendre des mesures immédiates et concrètes, afin d’éviter que cette crise financière ne se transforme en une crise sanitaire nationale.» I. items.title: Fleeing murder suspect crashes into elephant in Sri Lanka
items.description: A Sri Lankan man suspected of fatally stabbing a woman was arrested on Friday after he crashed his scooter into a wild elephant as he attempted to escape, police said. The 49-year-old man is accused of stabbing the woman in her home in the northern district of Anuradhapura, a police official told AFP . However, his attempted escape ended when his scooter crashed into the elephant as it emerged from the jungle onto the road a short distance away, the official said. Witnesses told police the elephant appeared to be unharmed and retreated into the jungle. The man was arrested and was receiving treatment for unspecified injuries under armed guard in hospital. Police also said they had recovered the suspected murder weapon. Encounters between humans and elephants are relatively common in Sri Lanka, where expanding settlements and farms often overlap with animal habitats. The island has recorded about 400 elephant and 150 human deaths annually over the past five years, according to official figures. Sri Lanka is home to an estimated 7,000 wild elephants and considers the animals a national treasure and they are protected by law. However, residents in remote villages sometimes attack elephants that destroy their crops.

items.title: Enseignement supérieur: le Premier ministre inaugure le siège de l’université virtuelle et deux espaces numériques ouverts
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ou é draogo, a proc é d é , ce jeudi 26 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, à l ’ inauguration du si è ge de l ’ Universit é virtuelle du Burkina Faso (UV-BF) et de deux Espaces numériques ouverts (ENO), situés à Bonheur-Ville et à Tampouy. Ces infrastructures s’inscrivent dans la dynamique de transformation du secteur éducatif impulsée par le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, avec pour ambition d’offrir à la jeunesse des conditions de formation adaptées aux exigences du monde contemporain. ‎Le siège de l’UV-BF est constitué d’un bâtiment de type R+4 avec sous-sol, complété par un plateau omnisports et des ouvrages communautaires. L’ensemble a nécessité un investissement de 6,9 milliards de francs CFA. Le bâtiment abrite notamment sept salles de réunion équipées pour la visioconférence, une salle polyvalente, 71 bureaux, un laboratoire de réalité virtuelle, un studio de production audiovisuelle, un mini-centre de données, une salle de monitoring et 28 locaux techniques. ‎Les ENO de Tampouy et de Bonheur-Ville, qui constituent des relais de proximité, ont nécessité un investissement de 3,2 milliards de francs CFA chacun. Chaque complexe comprend notamment un amphithéâtre pouvant accueillir jusqu’à 300 personnes, deux espaces de travail ouverts, une salle de formation, des bureaux et plusieurs locaux techniques. ‎Pour le Premier ministre, ces réalisations traduisent la volonté affirmée des autorités de faire de la formation du capital humain une priorité nationale. « Ce sont des investissements inédits qui permettent aujourd’hui de moderniser l’offre d’enseignement, d’accroître les capacités d’accueil et surtout de consolider et d’affirmer davantage la place centrale accordée à la formation de la jeunesse dans la Révolution progressiste populaire », a-t-il souligné. ‎Au-delà de leur dimension infrastructurelle, ces réalisations constituent une réponse concrète aux défis liés à l’accessibilité géographique et sociale de l’enseignement supérieur. Elles offrent aux étudiants de meilleures conditions de formation et contribuent à réduire les disparités entre les apprenants des grandes villes et ceux des localités éloignées. ‎Dans son intervention, le Camarade ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation, Pr. Ardjouma Thiombiano, a expliqué que ce dispositif vise à garantir une formation accessible à tous, sans distinction de lieu de résidence ou de condition sociale. « L’objectif est de faire en sorte qu’aucun étudiant, aucun enfant du Burkina Faso ne soit exclu de la formation en raison de l’éloignement géographique ou de difficultés sociales », a-t-il indiqué. ‎Le ministre a également mis en avant les possibilités qu’offre l’enseignement à distance pour mobiliser les compétences. Outre les enseignants intervenant depuis le siège de l’Université, le dispositif permet de solliciter des enseignants-chercheurs d’autres institutions, notamment ceux de la diaspora et des universités étrangères. ‎Au nom des étudiants, le Camarade Tindegma Zongo a salué la réalisation de ces infrastructures, qui apportent des réponses à plusieurs difficultés rencontrées par les apprenants inscrits dans les formations à distance. Il a notamment évoqué les contraintes liées à l’accès aux équipements informatiques, à la connexion Internet et à l’accompagnement pédagogique. ‎« Désormais, l’Université virtuelle a un visage et des lieux où se retrouver », s’est-il réjoui. Au nom de ses camarades, il a pris l’engagement de contribuer à la préservation de ces infrastructures par la discipline, la responsabilité et la recherche de l’excellence. ‎Pour sa part, le président de l’Université virtuelle du Burkina Faso, Oumarou Zalé, a exprimé sa reconnaissance aux plus hautes autorités du pays pour leur accompagnement dans la concrétisation de ces projets. Il a souligné que ces réalisations constituent un tournant important dans le développement de l’institution. Elles lui permettront de disposer d’un cadre de travail approprié pour renforcer ses capacités opérationnelles et améliorer l’accompagnement des étudiants. ‎L’Université virtuelle du Burkina Faso a pour mission de promouvoir un enseignement supérieur performant et compétitif, fondé sur les technologies de l’information et de la communication ainsi que sur l’enseignement à distance. Son siège constitue le centre de pilotage où sont conçus et produits les contenus pédagogiques destinés aux étudiants de l’ensemble du territoire national. Les ENO servent de relais de proximité. ‎D’autres infrastructures sont annoncées dans les prochaines semaines, notamment à Bobo-Dioulasso, Koudougou, Fada N’Gourma et Ziniaré. À terme, l’ambition est de doter chaque région du Burkina Faso d’au moins un Espace numérique ouvert, afin de rapprocher l’offre de formation des populations et de renforcer l’équité territoriale. DCRP/Primature L’article Enseignement supérieur: le Premier ministre inaugure le siège de l'université virtuelle et deux espaces numériques ouverts est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: 2027 Election:​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​‍‌‌​‍‍‌​ INEC procures 57,000 new BVAS devices
items.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, says the commission has procured 57,000 new BVAS for the 2027 general elections. Prof. Amupitan disclosed this on Thursday during a sensitisation seminar by the Diocese of Abuja, Anglican Communion, on Civil and Political Education with the theme “Why Your Vote Still Matters” Represented by the Deputy Director, Voter Education and Publicity, Mr Wilfred Ifogah, Prof. Amupitan said that the commission had also reduced the threshold from 1,250 to 850 voters per machine and cleaned the register through biometric audit. He said that with 51 days to the Jan. 16, 2027, presidential and National Assembly elections, civic responsibility must not be outsourced. Amupitan said INEC would on Saturday conduct a nationwide mock accreditation exercise in two polling units per ward to test upgrades ahead of 2027. According to him, over 10.77 million new registrants were recorded during the Continuous Voter Registration, while over 1.6 million invalid records were removed, bringing the verified register to over 100 million voters, including 232,658 persons with disabilities. He said INEC had also upgraded its Result Viewing Portal, IReV, with automated checks for over-voting and arithmetic consistency on Form EC8A before transmission. The INEC boss urged citizens to resist vote buying, divisive politics and inflammatory language, noting that Sections 95, 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026 prescribe stiff penalties for electoral violence and hate speech. Also speaking, a legal practitioner, Mr Emeka Etiaba, SAN, said over-judicialisation of elections was eroding public confidence. Etiaba said trust is earned, not commanded, stressing that INEC and the judiciary must deliver credible processes in 2027 to restore confidence. He noted that technicalities, poor petition drafting and non-justiciable innovations often deny determination of cases on merit, leaving a few judges to decide outcomes involving thousands of voters. He said innovations such as AI validation on IReV, though laudable administratively, must be backed by law to be enforceable in court. Speaking at the event, the Primate of the Church of Nigeria, Anglican Communion, Most Rev. Henry Ndukuba, urged Nigerians, especially youths, to actively participate in the 2027 general elections. According to him, their votes remain critical to deepening democracy and national development. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the seminar is part of activities marking the 37th anniversary of the diocese and Carnival for Christ 2026. Ndukuba said the church organised the seminar to sensitise citizens on their civic responsibility ahead of the polls, and the 2027 electioneering campaigns were already underway, with general elections scheduled for January 2027. He said the church deemed it important to engage stakeholders in the electoral process to educate citizens on the need to make informed decisions. “Most of our citizens have lost confidence in our democratic processes. The church was committed to mobilising Nigerians to register, verify their names when INEC publishes the voters’ list and vote on Election Day.” According to him, politics concerns the distribution and management of national resources, care for citizens and opportunities for young people; hence the need for all Nigerians to be involved. “Nigeria is for all of us, no matter your religion or background. We have the right to determine who leads us,” Ndukuba said. On her part, Senior Manager, YIAGA Africa, Ms Safiya Bichi, urged young people to move beyond social media activism to actual voting and mobilisation. “Whether you turn out to vote or not, you have made a decision. Votes are decided by those who turn out,” she said. Bichi said if votes were not valuable, politicians would not buy them, urging young Christians and urban voters to participate actively. NAN also reports that the Diocese of Abuja is marking 37 years of pastoral ministry, community service and moral witness, with the carnival focusing on faith, citizenship and responsible participation in national life. items.description: Countries: Sudan, Central African Republic, Chad, Egypt, Ethiopia, Libya, South Sudan, Uganda Source: UN High Commissioner for Refugees Please refer to the attached file. Situation and Operational Response SUDAN Key developments ▪ Poor rainfall, harvest failures and continued insecurity across parts of Darfur and eastern Sudan deepened food insecurity and livelihood pressures, contributing to further displacement and increasing humanitarian needs. Rising tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea and continued insecurity in South Sudan heightened the risk of new cross-border movements into Sudan, prompting UNHCR, the Commissioner for Refugees (COR) and partners to maintain border monitoring and preparedness for potential new arrivals. ▪ UNHCR and partners sustained protection and assistance, including registration, legal aid and returnee support in Blue Nile State, despite insecurity, aerial threats, movement constraints and fuel shortages. In October, missions to White Nile, Kassala and Northern States assessed protection needs, strengthened coordination and supported refugee-hosting and returnee communities. An ECHO mission underscored unmet refugee protection needs and the role of Multi-Purpose Community Centres (MPCCs) in delivering integrated services, while joint missions with the Assistant Commissioner for Refugees (ACOR) helped strengthen support for reception and protection assistance for returnees from Egypt. Population Movements, Registration and Relocation As of 31 October 2026, Sudan hosted more than 921,000 refugees and asylum-seekers, primarily from South Sudan, Eritrea and Ethiopia. Nearly 40,000 new arrivals were recorded in 2026, with White Nile, Kassala, Darfur, Blue Nile, Kordofan and Gedaref hosting the largest numbers. White Nile alone received nearly 3,800 new arrivals from South Sudan in October. In 2026, UNHCR and COR issued or renewed identification documents for nearly 119,000 refugees and asylum-seekers, supporting access to legal status, services and assistance. In White Nile, nearly 2,900 refugees received Foreigner Identification Numbers (FINs), while the issuance of refugee identity cards began, advancing the integration of refugee identity management into national systems. Nearly 8.6 million people remain internally displaced in Sudan. Despite a slight decline in overall displacement, insecurity continued to drive new movements in Blue Nile, Darfur, Kordofan and Northern States. In Blue Nile alone, nearly 120,000 people have been displaced since January, increasing pressure on host communities, gathering sites, schools and public buildings. Returns also continued, with more than 4.3 million people returning to their areas of origin within Sudan, mainly in Khartoum and Aj Jazirah. UNHCR estimates that approximately 1.37 million Sudanese have also returned from neighbouring countries since 2024, primarily from Egypt, South Sudan and Chad. Many returnees, however, face significant challenges due to limited resources, damaged infrastructure and unmet shelter, health, water and food needs. UNHCR and the Sudanese Red Crescent Society (SRCS) recorded more than 46,600 Sudanese returning from Egypt in October. Reported protection concerns included arbitrary detention, physical abuse, family separation and confiscation of documents and belongings, underscoring the need for continued protection monitoring and assistance at border entry points. UNHCR and partners’ response Registration, verification and documentation supported refugees and displaced families to maintain legal status and access assistance. In Gedaref, registration resumed in Um Gargour and Um Rakuba camps, with 137 refugees registered, more than 300 children added to family records, nearly 2,000 proof-ofregistration documents updated and 300 biometric records updated. Registration and verification also continued across Blue Nile, White Nile, Red Sea, Northern and North Kordofan States, supporting identification of needs, assistance planning and updated records for displaced and refugee households. Mental health and psychosocial support reached more than 19,200 refugees, returnees, IDPs and host communities across Sudan. In Khartoum, nearly 500 consultations and therapy sessions supported around 260 vulnerable people, mainly women and girls, while Northern State recorded nearly 500 counselling sessions and over 220 referrals for specialized care. Community-based protection activities reached more than 20,600 people with protection awareness and mine-risk education. Protection monitoring in Darfur identified risks linked to food insecurity, displacement and violence against women and girls, while activities in White Nile and Kassala strengthened access to protection services, referrals and food assistance. More than 50 survivors of Gender Based Violence (GBV) received psychosocial support and referrals, while child protection activities reached over 5,300 children and supported 95 at-risk children through Best Interests Assessments. Interventions also addressed child recruitment and labour, while training strengthened safe referrals and survivor-centred responses. Over 1,100 people received legal representation, counselling and consultations, while legal awareness activities reached over 3,500 people. In Blue Nile, mobile courts facilitated more than 1,160 civil documents, while legal aid, detention monitoring and advocacy supported access to justice, the release of detained refugees and protection assistance for trafficking survivors. Support to 19 refugee- and displaced people-led organizations strengthened community resilience and locally led solutions, including education, peacebuilding, water access and social inclusion initiatives. Activities benefited 250 children through new classrooms and reached more than 2,500 people through peacebuilding, while rehabilitation of the Hegliga Multi-Purpose Community Centre in Khartoum began to support recovery, skills development and access to services. Emergency preparedness and response addressed urgent needs, while strengthening local response capacity. In Central Darfur, 1,200 displaced households received relief items, with additional supplies dispatched across Darfur. In Gedaref, more than 200 refugee households received shelter and relief support, while 80 displaced households received family tents and 250 vulnerable households received cash assistance in Northern State. Response efforts in Blue Nile and Tawila supported assessments, referrals, reception arrangements and newly displaced families, while community fire-watch groups in Al Afad helped contain a fire and prevent wider shelter damage. Access to essential services remained critical for refugees and host communities. Nearly 52,000 people accessed water, sanitation, health and nutrition services in Gedaref refugee camps, including almost 6,700 medical consultations. Food assistance reached more than 35,000 refugees, while over 1,300 hot meals supported newly arrived asylum-seekers. Rehabilitation of water infrastructure, health facilities and schools in Gedaref, East Darfur and Red Sea States further improved access to basic services.

items.title: World: Hunger Hotspots FAO-WFP early warnings on acute food insecurity December 2026 to May 2027 outlook
items.description: Countries: World, Afghanistan, Chad, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Madagascar, Mali, Myanmar, Nigeria, occupied Palestinian territory, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Uganda, Yemen Sources: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, World Food Programme Please refer to the attached file. El Niño Adds New Hunger Hotspots as Conflict Continues to Drive Risk of Famine, Warn FAO and WFP | World Food Programme Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, parts of Nigeria and Yemen remain hotspots of highest concern with Southern Africa and the Central American Dry Corridor among new additions ROME – El Niño has pushed Southern Africa and the Central American Dry Corridor onto the list of hunger hotspots, where acute food insecurity is projected to worsen significantly between December 2026 and May 2027, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) warned today. In their latest Hunger Hotspots report , the agencies also identified a risk of famine in parts of Sudan and South Sudan. The report, released twice a year through the Global Network Against Food Crises, lists 16 hotspots, up from 13 in June. El Niño is a major driver behind three of the four newly identified hotspots: Southern Africa (Eswatini, Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia and Zimbabwe), the Central American Dry Corridor and northeastern Uganda. Chad has been added to the list due to the continued spillover effects of the conflict in neighbouring Sudan. El Niño is gaining strength and could prove one of the most intense on record. In Southern Africa, drier and hotter conditions threaten planting, farm work and future harvests. Up to 3 million people in Zimbabwe, 2.6 million in Malawi and 1.8 million in Mozambique are projected to face high levels of acute food insecurity in the months ahead, through to March 2027. In the Central American Dry Corridor, the 2026 Primera season, known as the first crop season, was the driest in four decades, and crop losses topped 75 percent in many areas. As food stocks run out, the 2027 lean season could start early. In Guatemala alone, 3.2 million people are projected to face high levels of acute food insecurity between October 2026 and February 2027. Acting before El Niño’s worst effects arrive can prevent damage to harvests, livestock and incomes. The joint FAO–WFP El Niño anticipatory action plan aims to protect 9 million people in 22 countries. Elsewhere, conflict and armed violence remain among the primary drivers of acute food insecurity in 12 of the 16 hotspots, including all five hotspots of highest concern: Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, parts of Nigeria and Yemen. In four of these five hotspots, the latest analyses identified or projected people facing Catastrophe, the most severe phase of the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), marked by starvation and death. In Somalia, although no population is currently projected to face Catastrophe (IPC Phase 5) and the risk of famine has receded, acute food insecurity remains at Emergency (IPC Phase 4) levels among displaced populations in Baidoa. The most severe situations are in Sudan and South Sudan, where the risk of famine has been identified. Under a reasonable worst-case scenario, there is a risk of famine in 13 areas of North Darfur and South Kordofan in Sudan through January 2027, while in two camps for displaced people in South Darfur, acute malnutrition levels have already exceeded famine thresholds. In South Sudan, the latest available analysis indicated a risk of famine in four counties of Upper Nile and Jonglei states through July 2026, under a worst-case scenario. All five hotspots of highest concern have repeatedly been at this level since 2022, yet funding for humanitarian assistance for food security and nutrition in these hotspots fell by 62 percent, from USD 5.1 billion in 2022 to USD 2.0 billion in 2025. Four additional hotspots are classified as being of very high concern: Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Haiti and Palestine. While food security in the Gaza Strip has started to improve after the October 2025 ceasefire, gains are fragile, and acute food insecurity in the West Bank is expected to worsen. FAO and WFP are calling for urgent humanitarian action across all 16 hotspots, above all where a risk of famine has been identified, and for safe, unimpeded access to people in need. “El Niño is intensifying, threatening crops and harvests in already vulnerable regions and increasing the risk of acute food insecurity,” said FAO Director-General QU Dongyu. “Yet the worst outcomes are not inevitable. Life-saving agricultural assistance to boost food production of highly vulnerable families is an essential part of the multi-sectoral response to the situations described in the report. That is where FAO is focused.” “I’ve called upon all nations to banish famine to the history books,” said WFP Executive Director Luke J. Lindberg. “This report tells us where famine could strike next, so the timing to follow through on our commitment is now. It will take a united effort to end conflicts, fully resource our WFP field teams, and ensure they have safe access to reach vulnerable communities. This is not a problem of operational ability, it is a question of whether world leaders have the political courage to act decisively.” # # # The 16 hunger hotspots Highest concern: Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, parts of Nigeria and Yemen. Very high concern: Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Haiti and Palestine. Other hotspots: Chad, the Central American Dry Corridor, Madagascar, Mali, Myanmar, Southern Africa (Eswatini, Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia and Zimbabwe) and northeastern Uganda. Chad, the Central American Dry Corridor, Southern Africa and northeastern Uganda are new to the list. Lebanon is no longer a hotspot. Note on IPC levels IPC Phase 3 refers to “crisis” levels of food insecurity, in which households either have food consumption gaps that are reflected by high or above-usual acute malnutrition, or are marginally able to meet minimum food needs but only by depleting essential livelihood assets or through crisis-coping strategies. IPC Phase 4 refers to “emergency” levels of food insecurity, in which households either have large food consumption gaps which are reflected in very high acute malnutrition and excess mortality, or are able to mitigate large food consumption gaps but only by employing emergency livelihood strategies and asset liquidation. IPC Phase 5 refers to “catastrophe/famine” levels of food insecurity, in which households have an extreme lack of food and/or other basic needs even after full employment of coping strategies. Starvation, death, destitution and extremely critical acute malnutrition levels are evident. At the household level, IPC Phase 5 is classified as Catastrophe, while famine is an area-level classification requiring evidence that thresholds for acute food insecurity, acute malnutrition and mortality have been met. The Cadre Harmonisé (CH), used in West Africa and the Sahel, uses the same phases. Notes to editors Identified through forward-looking analysis, hunger hotspots are areas where acute food insecurity is likely to deteriorate significantly during the outlook period. They are selected through a consensus-based process involving FAO and WFP field and technical teams, alongside analysts specialized in conflict, economic risks and natural hazards. The report is produced with financial support from the European Union through the Global Network Against Food Crises. The full report can be accessed here . B-roll and shotlist can be accessed here . Photos can be accessed here . The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) is a specialized agency that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. Its goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. FAO works across more than 130 countries to transform agrifood systems, making them more efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable. The United Nations World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of weather extremes.

items.title: Burkina Faso seeks Nigeria’s partnership against terrorism, trafficking
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Burkina Faso has pledged to strengthen security cooperation with Nigeria to tackle terrorism, drug trafficking, human trafficking and other cross-border crimes threatening stability in West Africa. Burkina Faso’s Minister of Security, Mahamadou Sana, made the commitment during a meeting with Nigeria’s Ambassador to the country, Syndoph Endoni, in Ouagadougou, according to a statement issued after the meeting. Sana said stronger bilateral cooperation would enable both countries to develop practical responses to terrorism and other transnational crimes. He commended Nigeria’s longstanding relationship with Burkina Faso, recalling its support over the years, particularly its contributions to the country’s 2015 electoral process. The minister also identified Nigeria’s industrial development as an area Burkina Faso could learn from, citing the Dangote Refinery as an example of the country’s growing industrial capacity. He stressed that peace and stability were essential to attracting investment and creating economic opportunities. Responding, Endoni said security and development were inseparable, warning that instability in one West African country could have consequences for its neighbours. “There is no development without peace and security and there is no peace and security without development,” the ambassador said. Describing the relationship between the two countries as deeper than conventional diplomacy, Endoni said their historical ties were founded on “fraternity and brotherhood.” He called for sustained dialogue and stronger bilateral engagement to address shared challenges, particularly transnational organised crime. The proposed areas of cooperation include intelligence sharing, operational coordination, capacity building and technology transfer, potentially involving Nigerian agencies such as NAPTIP, NDLEA, NITDA, NIPC and the Bank of Industry, alongside their Burkinabe counterparts. The post Burkina Faso seeks Nigeria’s partnership against terrorism, trafficking appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Flash floods cut families off from healthcare in Mudug, Somalia
items.description: Country: Somalia Source: Médecins Sans Frontières Flash flooding from heavy Deyr rains has affected more than 20,000 households in Galmudug, including in Galkayo, according to the state authorities. In Galkayo, floodwater has cut roads across the town, making it harder and more expensive for families to reach MSF-supported Mudug Regional Hospital and Galkayo TB Hospital. Cases of acute watery diarrhoea at MSF-supported facilities in Mudug more than doubled, from 356 in October 2025 to 748 in October 2026, and two cholera cases have been confirmed at Mudug Regional Hospital. Nearly two in three children admitted to the inpatient malnutrition ward in early November had acute watery diarrhoea. Our teams have expanded the ward from 28 to 70 beds, strengthened disease surveillance, trained staff on cholera, dengue and measles, and are reinforcing our capacity to treat cholera cases. ​ Flash floods are hitting towns across central Somalia, yet flood preparedness and limited available funding focus mainly on river flooding. Repairs In places such as Mudug, resources for responding to flash floods remain insufficient, leaving little for the drainage, safe water and sanitation that would protect families’ access to healthcare through the next rains. Humanitarian funding cuts are also leaving families across Somalia further from care. MSF calls on donors to make flexible funding available for the wider response to flash floods in areas such as Mudug, not only to riverine floods. MSF also calls on health authorities and humanitarian organisations to strengthen a coordinated response to urgent health, water and sanitation needs, and to invest in health facilities that can keep functioning through future floods. Families in Galkayo should not lose access to healthcare because the flood that reached them came from heavy rain rather than a river. For 15 days, Farhia Hassan Aden’s 18-month-old son had been vomiting and had diarrhoea. There is no clinic in her village in Mudug region, and since the October rains the motorised rickshaws that carry families to hospital have not been able to get through the water. The fare, US$4 to 5, was more than the family could pay. So Farhia walked through the floodwater with her son to Mudug Regional Hospital in Galkayo, which Doctors Without Borders/ Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) supports. He was admitted. “It forced us to walk in the water with our sick children,” she says. Farhia’s family is one of many caught by flash flooding since the Deyr rains began in October, in a year of El Niño conditions. In one week in October, more than 20,000 households were affected across Galmudug, including in Galkayo district, according to the authorities. Cut off and falling ill For five days, Bisharo Badal Yusuf could not get her 14-month-old son to hospital. He was vomiting and had diarrhoea, but floodwater had cut the roads. “We are cut off, which has forced families to keep sick children at home,” she says. “I eventually brought him to the hospital in critical condition.” Two days into his treatment, his fever had come down. Standing floodwater is also making people ill. Toilets have overflowed, floodwater has mixed with sewage, and the stagnant water that collects between houses fills with flies and mosquitoes. “The children are constantly scratching, and insects are swarming around them,” says Farhia. What our teams are seeing In October 2026, our teams recorded 748 cases of acute watery diarrhoea at MSF-supported facilities in Mudug, more than double the 356 in October 2025. Some patients have travelled more than 200 kilometres for care. In early November, admissions to the inpatient malnutrition ward at Mudug Regional Hospital were almost double last year’s, and nearly two in three children admitted had acute watery diarrhoea. We have expanded the ward from 28 to 70 beds. MSF works alongside the Ministry of Health at Mudug Regional Hospital and Galkayo Hospital, supporting emergency, maternity, neonatal and paediatric care, treatment for children with severe acute malnutrition, tuberculosis care and community health activities, all free of charge. Since the rains began, we have added staff, strengthened disease surveillance, trained teams on cholera, dengue and measles, and put supplies in place. Two cholera cases have now been confirmed at Mudug Regional Hospital. With the health authorities, our teams are strengthening cholera case management and sending mobile clinics to the communities hit hardest. Fewer places to turn For a family that, in Farhia’s words, “cannot even afford a single tablet of medicine”, each closure means a longer journey and a higher fare, and free care far away can be out of reach even before the roads flood. “Funding has been shrinking across the whole of Somalia, and access to healthcare with it,” says Dr Janvier Bahati, MSF project medical referent in Mudug. “In the long run, El Niño will make the current situation worse, reducing people’s capacity to cope, to the point where they are vulnerable to disease and malnutrition.” What families are asking for Asked what would help, the mothers we spoke to named simple things. Farhia wants the mosquitoes sprayed and the floodwater pumped out. Bisharo wants sanitation improved and “channels for the water”. “What the humanitarian actors need to focus on is to make sure that communities far away, and those affected by the flood, also have access to services,” says Bahati. “For me, that is the call: a drainage system across the city, chlorination of water and distribution of Aquatabs at community level.” Yet flood preparedness has focused largely on the river basins, leaving little for drainage, safe water and sanitation in places such as Mudug. MSF calls on donors to make flexible funding available for the wider response to flash floods in areas such as Mudug, not only to riverine floods. MSF also calls on health authorities and humanitarian organisations to strengthen a coordinated response to urgent health, water and sanitation needs, and to invest in health facilities that can keep functioning through future floods. John Riaga Media Manager Email: john.riaga@nairobi.msf.org Website: msf.or.ke

items.title: WFP South Sudan Country Brief (November 2026)
items.description: Country: South Sudan Source: World Food Programme Please refer to the attached file. Assistance and access: WFP reached about half a million people, distributed 2,343 metric tonnes of food and transferred USD 1.58 million in cash. Insecurity delayed deliveries in parts of Upper Nile and Jonglei, and reduced air transport capacity from November threatens deliveries to remote communities. Famine prevention: WFP had funding from November for only three of six priority counties: Ulang, Nasir and Nyirol. Uror, Fangak and Akobo still lacked funding for the response. WFP reported an overall funding shortfall of USD 388 million for October 2026–March 2027. Acute malnutrition: October surveys recorded rates of 28.3% in Fangak and 22.8% in Leer, both above the 15% emergency threshold. In Akobo, WFP worked with UNICEF and IRC to keep 14 supplementary feeding sites operating through December.

items.title: Conakry Terminal accélère ses investissements : 82,6 millions d’euros mobilisés pour l’extension des quais
items.description: Une ambition portée en cohérence avec la vision des autorités guinéennes : doter le pays d’un port moderne, compétitif et prêt pour le programme Simandou 2040. Conakry, le 26 novembre 2026 – Conakry Terminal, filiale du groupe AGL, franchit une nouvelle étape dans le renforcement de ses infrastructures avec la signature d’une convention de financement de 82,6 millions d’euros avec AFG Bank et Ecobank, destinée au développement de quais supplémentaires. Cette opération accélère les projets de développement du terminal et s’inscrit pleinement dans la vision portée par le Gouvernement guinéen pour la modernisation du Port de Conakry et de l’économie nationale. Partenaire stratégique du Port de Conakry, Conakry Terminal n’a pas attendu la réalisation des travaux de dragage préalables pour lancer le projet d’extension. Sur un investissement global de 341 millions d’euros, 85,2 millions d’euros ont déjà été mobilisés et préfinancés sur fonds propres. La convention signée avec AFG Bank et Ecobank prend désormais le relais pour financer la suite du projet. La convention a été signée par Édouard LENO, Directeur Général de Conakry Terminal, Sayouba OUEDRAOGO, Directeur Général d’AFG Bank, et Diawadou BAH, Directeur Général d’Ecobank. Le projet du Quai 14 permettra de renforcer les capacités opérationnelles du terminal, d’améliorer la qualité et la fluidité des opérations portuaires et d’anticiper les volumes attendus avec les nombreux mégaprojets du programme Simandou 2040, en phase avec les priorités de développement fixées par les autorités. À cette occasion, Édouard LENO, Directeur Général de Conakry Terminal, a déclaré : « Le projet du Quai 14 traduit notre engagement dans la durée en faveur du développement et de la modernisation du Port de Conakry. Nous avons engagé les investissements nécessaires et démarré avec anticipation ce chantier majeur. La mise en place de ce préfinancement constitue une nouvelle étape dans la réalisation de ce projet structurant. Nous saluons la confiance d’AFG Bank et d’Ecobank, qui nous accompagnent dans la poursuite de cet investissement au service de la performance du port et de l’économie guinéenne. » Au-delà du Quai 14, Conakry Terminal a déjà lancé les études du Quai 16, qui ajoutera 400 mètres de linéaire de quai et devrait mobiliser près de 400 millions d’euros d’investissements supplémentaires. Diawadou BAH, Directeur Général d’Ecobank Guinée, a salué ce partenariat : « Ecobank est fière d’accompagner Conakry Terminal dans la réalisation du projet stratégique du Quai 14. Ce préfinancement est le gage de notre engagement continu à soutenir les investissements structurants qui contribuent à renforcer la compétitivité de la Guinée, à favoriser le développement du commerce et à contribuer durablement à la croissance économique du pays. » De son côté, Abdourahim BAH, Directeur Commercial d’AFG Bank Guinée, a souligné la continuité de l’engagement de la banque :Sensitivity: Internal « En tant que partenaire bancaire historique de Conakry Terminal, AFG Bank Guinée est particulièrement fière d’accompagner cette nouvelle phase de son développement. Après avoir soutenu la première extension du Terminal à Conteneurs en 2014 ainsi que plusieurs programmes d’acquisition d’équipements majeurs ces dernières années, notre participation à ce financement pour le Quai 14 illustre la continuité de notre engagement. Le financement par AFG de cet investissement structurant pour le pays démontre notre capacité d’exécution sur des transactions à très forte valeur ajoutée et notre volonté de soutenir durablement la modernisation des infrastructures critiques pour la croissance économique de la Guinée. » Cette opération témoigne de la confiance des partenaires financiers d’AGL dans la solidité et les perspectives de ses projets, ainsi que de leur volonté d’accompagner des investissements structurants au service de l’économie nationale. La vision d’AGL est claire : en accélérant ses investissements, l’entreprise confirme son engagement à bâtir des infrastructures logistiques solides, alignées sur l’ambitieux programme de développement de la Guinée, Simandou 2040. items.title: UN warns famine risks rising as hunger hotspots increase
items.description: By Clara Schoenthaler ROME, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Hunger is set to worsen significantly in 16 global hotspots over the coming six months, with famine threatening parts of Africa, two United Nations agencies warned on Friday. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and World Food Programme (WFP) said Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen faced the gravest threats, driven by conflict, displacement, economic hardship and extreme weather.

items.title: Espagne : comment le Maroc occupe une place centrale dans le débat électoral
items.description: Dans deux jours, les Espagnols se rendront aux urnes pour les élections législatives anticipées. Le Maroc, sous différentes formes, figure parmi les principaux sujets de la campagne en cours dans le pays ibérique. Alors que les Espagnols se préparent à renouveler les Cortes Generales dimanche, en élisant 350 élus au Congrès des députés et les membres du Sénat (208 élus au suffrage direct), les partis politiques ont utilisé le Maroc dans plusieurs de leurs argumentaires de campagne et parfois dans leur programme. Selon un récent sondage Cluster 17, cité par les médias, plus d’un tiers (34%) des électeurs sondés estiment que la relation de Madrid avec le Maroc constitue le sujet international qui pourrait le plus influencer leur vote, tandis que près de la moitié affirment que les sujets internationaux n'influenceront pas leur vote. « Les relations avec le Maroc et la situation à Sebta et Melilla sont, parmi les sujets internationaux, celles qui pourraient le plus influencer le vote » , a indiqué Legrandcontinent, tandis que la relation avec les États-Unis n’est quant à elle citée que par 9 % des électeurs, le conflit au Proche-Orient par 8 %, et la guerre en Ukraine et les questions de dépenses de défense par 4 %. Appels à la suspension des relations commerciales avec le Maroc Jeudi, un membre de l'extrême droite espagnol (Vox), a appelé à la suspension des relations commerciales avec le Maroc, ainsi que de tous « les financements européens destinés au pays afin de protéger le secteur primaire espagnol », selon The Objective. Jorge Buxadé, député européen, chef de la délégation de Vox à Bruxelles, a également demandé le « renforcement des contrôles aux frontières dans les ports espagnols afin de protéger les zones rurales et de garantir la sécurité alimentaire », dans une idée d'asphyxier les exportations marocaines et les empêcher de faire concurrence aux produits espagnols. Ces déclarations ont été tenues à l'occasion de la deuxième édition des « Petits déjeuners à la campagne », où le député d'extrême droite a plaidé pour une « préférence communautaire » et à mettre un terme à la concurrence. « Ils ont envahi une partie du territoire espagnol. Un point c’est tout. Tant que cette situation ne sera pas résolue, tant que vous ne serez pas tous rentrés dans votre pays, tant que vous ne respecterez pas un État membre, à savoir l’Espagne, les relations commerciales sont suspendues et, bien entendu, toute aide financière accordée au Maroc est suspendue », a-t-il déclaré. Sebta et Melilla comme thèmes de campagne Par ailleurs, la droite et l'extrême droite espagnoles misent sur les événements migratoires de Sebta pour tenter d'arracher des points dans les sondages ou plus encore, espérer une victoire face aux socialistes représentés par Pedro Sanchez. En effet, l'immigration s'annonce comme un thème central de cette campagne aux côtés, des enclaves occupées de Sebta et Melilla, et du Mondial 2030, laissant les sujets relatifs à la crise sociale et économique, les politiques publiques, européennes, reléguées au second rang. Les problèmes de communication constatés entre les différentes institutions de renseignement en Espagne ayant précédé les événements migratoires de Sebta, l'impossibilité du côté de Madrid de savoir comment ont été initiés ces mouvements et par quelles parties, a favorisé un discours simpliste, d'accusation visant Rabat comme instigateur chez l'extrême droite et une partie des médias ibériques qui ont préféré trouver un « ennemi » prêt à l’emploi au lieu d'investiguer sur ces événements qui ont choqué au Maroc aussi, où au même moment, était célébrée la Fête du Trône. La co-organisation de la Coupe du Monde 2030 Le Maroc figure aussi en tant que thème et sujet de la campagne électorale espagnole dans le sport. Le Mondial 2030 et plus précisément qui de l'Espagne et le Maroc, abritera la finale de la compétition, fait l'objet de prises de positions osées et étonnantes chez les acteurs politiques. Le Premier ministre sortant, Pedro Sanchez, a changé de position dans ce cadre en passant par un respect de la décision de la FIFA à faire des déclarations teintées de certitude que la finale serait jouée en Espagne plutôt qu'au Maroc. Dans un entretien accordé à Mundo Deportivo, il a assuré que « la finale de la Coupe du monde 2030 se déroulera en Espagne ». D'autres partis politiques ibériques, comme Vox de l'extrême droite ou encore Podemos et Sumar de l'extrême gauche, se sont invités au débat cet été en se prêtant au jeu de la bataille politico-sportive. Ils ont voulu profiter de la crise migratoire de Sebta pour tenter de faire retirer au Maroc l'organisation du Mondial 2030, alors même que le dossier espagnol n'avait aucune chance d'être sélectionné par la FIFA sans le Maroc, en témoignent les nombreuses tentatives espagnoles infructueuses précédentes. De son côté, toujours en utilisant le thème du Mondial pour se positionner dans le scrutin, Alberto Nuñez Feijoo, candidat du Parti populaire (PP, droite), est allé plus loin en se rendant sur le terrain de la menace. « Si je suis président du gouvernement et que la finale n'a pas lieu en Espagne, notre pays n'accueillera pas la Coupe du monde » , a-t-il déclaré. Pour rappel, trois stades sont en lice pour accueillir la finale, le Camp Nou à Barcelone, le Bernabeu à Madrid et le futur stade Hassan II à Benslimane, construit pour le Mondial et qui est, des trois, le plus grand stade en termes de capacité d'accueil. The post Espagne : comment le Maroc occupe une place centrale dans le débat électoral appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Questions about Tinubu’s identity come up anytime he’s about to win election — Fashola
items.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has dismissed renewed questions about President Bola Tinubu’s background and identity, saying the controversies resurface whenever the president is on the verge of winning an election. Fashola described the questions as needless distractions, insisting that Tinubu had met the constitutional requirements to contest the presidency and that Nigerians had already settled the matter through their votes. He said the controversy had persisted for more than two decades but had not stopped Tinubu from winning elections, expressing confidence that the president would secure another victory in 2027. Fashola spoke in an interview with ARISE News while responding to questions about the perceived secrecy surrounding Tinubu’s background and identity. “I think that these matters have carried on for all of 20-something years. So, every time he’s at the threshold of winning an election, these issues come, and you know what always happens: he wins,” he said. “So history is about to repeat itself again. He’s going to win. These are needless distractions. They don’t answer a fundamental question. And I’ve said about minimum qualification. He has met it,” the former governor added. Fashola questioned the relevance of the controversies to Nigerians, saying opposition politicians should focus on issues that would improve the lives of citizens rather than repeatedly raising questions about Tinubu’s background. “The question I will focus upon if I were those fragmented opposition is how does this help the people whose mandate I want? It doesn’t help them,” he said. The former minister of works also argued that some of the issues had previously been subjected to legal proceedings and investigations, including during the 1999 political period and the last presidential election. Drawing on his experience as a legal practitioner, Fashola said there was a need to allow an end to prolonged disputes, invoking the legal principle that litigation must eventually come to a conclusion. “I believe parts of this were litigated in the last election. They were litigated in 1999. It was the subject of a House investigation in that period. You keep referring to my other life as a legal practitioner, there’s a principle in that life. There’s something we say, a principle that there must be an end to litigation. It’s enough,” he said. Fashola said Nigerians had moved on from the controversy, citing Tinubu’s victory in the 2023 presidential election as evidence, and predicted that voters would reaffirm their position in 2027. “They pursue it at their own choice, but I think the Nigerian people have left that subject behind. They have left it behind with their votes in 2023. They will reaffirm it in 2027,” he said. items.title: Coupe de la CAF : Le Raja et l’AS FAR face à des défis contrastés en phase de groupes
items.description: Le Raja Casablanca et l'AS FAR entament samedi leur parcours en phase de groupes de la Coupe de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF), avec l’ambition de défendre les chances du football marocain et de franchir le cap des quarts de finale, dans une compétition où les deux représentants nationaux devront composer avec des adversaires de calibre différent. L’AS FAR, versée dans le groupe B, accueillera la formation sud-africaine de Durban City FC, pour une première sortie qui constitue une occasion importante de prendre les commandes de sa poule. Les Militaires retrouveront également l’Azam FC de Tanzanie et Al Ahly Tripoli de Libye, deux formations qui disposent d’une expérience appréciable sur la scène continentale. Sur le papier, le groupe B apparaît ouvert, même si l’AS FAR possède des arguments sérieux pour viser la qualification. Forte de son expérience africaine et de son statut parmi les clubs marocains les plus compétitifs, la formation rbatie peut légitimement ambitionner l’une des deux premières places. Elle devra toutefois se montrer régulière, notamment lors de ses déplacements en Tanzanie et en Libye, face à des adversaires susceptibles de lui disputer la première place. Le Raja Casablanca, engagé dans le groupe A, sera également au rendez-vous samedi face à l’ASKO de Kara du Togo. Les Verts auront toutefois fort à faire dans une poule particulièrement relevée, qui comprend également Al Ahly d’Égypte et Primeiro de Agosto d’Angola. Le duel avec Al Ahly, l’un des clubs les plus titrés du continent et habitué aux grands rendez-vous africains, s’annonce comme l’un des principaux obstacles sur la route des Casablancais. Primeiro de Agosto, formation angolaise rompue aux compétitions continentales, constitue également un concurrent sérieux. Le Raja dispose néanmoins d’un potentiel sportif et d’un vécu continental qui lui permettent d’aborder cette phase avec ambition. La confrontation directe avec Al Ahly pourrait notamment peser dans la course à la première place, tandis que les deux rencontres face à Primeiro de Agosto seront déterminantes. Pour les deux clubs marocains, une victoire lors de cette première journée serait un signal fort dans la course à la qualification, les deux premiers de chaque groupe devant accéder aux quarts de finale. items.title: ECP says it cannot force parties to field women on winnable seats
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Friday made it clear that the allocation of party tickets was an internal matter for political parties and that it had no legal authority to intervene. The ECP explained its position a day after a National Assembly panel directed it to ensure that the five per cent quota for women on general seats under Section 206 of the Elections Act, 2017, is implemented in a manner that women are fielded on seats where their victory is certain. The ECP said it had informed the Sub-Committee of the National Assembly’s Special Committee on Gender Mainstreaming at the time that, under the existing electoral laws, the authority to award tickets to women rested with the political party concerned. According to the commission, ‘‘it could neither interfere in the process of ticket distribution nor decide on which seat a party should field a woman candidate”. The distribution of seats, the ECP said, was an internal affair of political parties. Therefore, if the committee wanted women to be given general seats where their victory was assured, legislation would be required for that purpose, and the power to legislate rested with Parliament. Section 206 of the Elections Act, 2017, requires every political party to award at least five per cent of its tickets on general seats to women candidates. The provision was introduced to increase women’s representation in elected bodies and ensure that parties do not confine women candidates to reserved seats alone. In practice, however, women candidates have often been fielded on seats considered difficult for their parties, a concern repeatedly raised in Parliament and by civil society organisations. The NA body has now urged the ECP to ensure that the quota translates into meaningful representation by requiring political parties to field women candidates in winnable constituencies. The ECP’s position is that the existing law only prescribes a minimum percentage of tickets for women. It does not empower the commission to assess the winnability of a constituency or direct a party to change its candidate for a particular seat. Legal experts say any such condition would require an amendment to the Elections Act by Parliament, specifying criteria for winnable seats and the mechanism for enforcement. The committee also directed the ECP to make arrangements for filling 563 vacant seats in various local governments. In this regard, the ECP informed the committee that it had issued election schedules on several occasions to fill these vacant seats. However, no woman had filed nomination papers for these seats, the commission said, adding that elections could not be held in the absence of candidates. The ECP said it remained ready to hold elections on vacant seats as soon as candidates came forward in accordance with the law. At Thursday’s meeting, the committee also reviewed a briefing by Nadra and noted that female registrations in 2026 were 5.57pc higher than male registrations. However, Senator Qaim Khani raised concerns over women’s representation in the authority’s senior management, where only 15 women held positions of director or above.

items.title: Chrysalis to butterfly: How Europe can help Serbia’s Student List spread its wings
items.description: Cover image: picture alliance / NurPhoto | Aleksandar Jovicic In William Butler’s novel, “The Butterfly Revolution”, a group of teenagers at a summer camp rise up against the management and take power. They demand more democracy and dignity, and an end to the old, corrupt rules. Serbia’s students won the country’s parliamentary election by a wide margin at the end of October; now they need to stay true to their goals of more democracy and better governance. This is especially pertinent since, according to ECFR interviews conducted in Serbia, the Student List is a mixed group—roughly half are pro-European, about a quarter are on the far left, and the rest are nationalist, which makes internal divisions more likely. What the student movement has achieved so far is remarkable. But Europe should not push Serbia to take new positions straight away on issues such as recognition of Kosovo or joining sanctions against Russia, lest it put a strain on the diverse student coalition. A movement built from below In November 2024, the canopy of Serbia’s Novi Sad railway station collapsed , killing 16 people. As well as underlying structural issues, the tragedy was attributed to government corruption and a lack of adequate oversight on a recent project to renovate the station’s roof. In the two years since, Serbia’s students created more than a protest network: their backlash against then president Aleksandar Vucic saw the Student List develop into a solid political movement. Its members chose individuals to run in the parliamentary election and the Student List governing programme was then written by working groups over an 18-month period. The party’s main goal is fixing Serbia’s myriad social and economic issues, since the country is mired in corruption ; its media have also long been under the control of Vucic. In order for the Student List to become a challenger in October’s election, students reached out to their parents, many of whom work in every institution and ministry, in every town and village, across the country. Students set up Viber groups, through which they mobilised their parents, grandparents and their grandparents’ neighbours to vote. The movement also interviewed and trained 60,000 election observers and polling station commission members, forming cross-country networks. This connectivity will be a major advantage for the Student List in the upcoming local elections, too—the date of which will be determined by Serbia’s pending new president. From chrysalis to butterfly From the middle of November, the Student List’s 140 MPs have 90 days to nominate a new prime minister and a government. The new cabinet faces difficult foreign policy tasks, and the prime minister will also have to try to patch up Serbia’s budget by unlocking EU payments under the Growth Plan for the Western Balkans and other European Commission instruments. In Belgrade, the chrysalis must now become a butterfly. Serbia’s students need to emerge from their safe, closed circle and spread their wings to enact the changes they have campaigned for since 2024. This will challenge how the group has made decisions so far: a prime minister needs autonomy but must stay true to the dignified spirit of the movement. Meanwhile, Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party sit in parliament, ready to accuse the Student List of incompetence and corruption, and of generally being unable to get anything done. View from the neighbourhood Serbia’s neighbours greeted the result of October 25th with cautious relief. Vucic’s fall removes a source of interference and disrupts the criminal networks that reached across the Western Balkans. But the Student List’s foreign policy programme suggests at least continuity in tone with Vucic’s previous approach to Kosovo and Russia. Even now, no Serbian politician will announce recognition for Kosovo, but the new government in Belgrade is the first in around 40 years with no personal legacy on the matter; it could begin tapering its control over Srpska Lista (Serb List), the main political party of the Serb minority in Kosovo, and criminal networks in northern Kosovo. Doing so would remove Pristina’s excuse not to engage. The government will also not join the EU sanctions on Russia, or at least not for now. The gas delivery contract with Gazprom is to be renewed this December, and Moscow will surely use its leverage. Elsewhere, Montenegro has the most to gain from the Student List’s win. It can hold its 2027 election without Serbian meddling, and it should see an end to entry bans on its journalists and public figures, and to Serbian attacks on its accession process. In Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Republika Srpska leadership—which had initially welcomed Serbia’s change in government—has become anxious because Vucic’s ally Milorad Dodik has no links to the Student List. While Dodik sells the Student List programme on Republika Srpska as aligning with his own positions, his relationship with Vucic ran on business and corruption networks; reform in Serbia would cut these, too. North Macedonia offers a warning. In 2016, the country’s “Colourful Revolution” defeated a seemingly entrenched elite , but the new government never dismantled the clientelist networks and the old ruling party returned to power in 2024. Winning against the system is thus not the same as dismantling it. In Serbia, the student generation does not see Bosnians, Kosovars or Albanians as threats. But the country’s foreign ministry is the most contested post, and nationalist rhetoric remains prescient. Serbia’s test for Europe For the first time in decades, Serbia can change the quality of its governance and stay on a pro-European path Nonetheless, Belgrade is in the position where it could lead regional reconciliation instead of continued alienation. For the first time in decades, Serbia can change the quality of its governance and stay on a pro-European path. Its other option is to fall back on its Yugoslav non-aligned instincts, which Russia would immediately exploit. Europeans need to be aware of this and approach the government’s pro-European voices with respect and humility. The EU can help improve Serbia’s anti-corruption reforms and support change in the country’s security services and media. But it needs to recognise just what the country’s students have pulled off. Europeans should give Serbians, and their new government, space to come to their own conclusions about foreign policy issues. By doing so, they can encourage the country down a path of wider reconciliation. The EU’s lesson in Serbia is that young people can be a powerful political engine—even as a minority in a country with an ageing population. They can defeat “strongman” rulers, of whom the Balkans have many. But Europeans also need to know when to take a step back and let new leadership take root. In Serbia, the students want to combine their networked organisation with a more dignified way of governing. Their butterfly wings will soon take shape. Source

items.title: Revue de presse de ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026
items.description: Voici les principaux titres développés par la presse nationale de ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026 L’Opinion Mondial 2030: 840.000 emplois attendus grâce aux investissements Le ministre de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et des Sports, Mohamed Mehdi Bensaïd, a indiqué novembre devant la Chambre des Conseillers que les investissements liés au Mondial 2030 devraient générer 840.000 emplois au Maroc, dont 52% dans le bâtiment et la construction. Présentant le budget sectoriel 2027 de son département devant la Commission de l’enseignement et des affaires culturelles et sociales, Mohamed Mehdi Bensaïd a détaillé la répartition de ces emplois. Le bâtiment et la construction en capteraient 52%, les autres industries 13,8% et l’hôtellerie-restauration 6,2%, les 28% restants se répartissant entre les autres secteurs. Al Bayane Benalilou souligne l’engagement du Maroc en faveur de la consécration des principes d’intégrité et des fondements de l’État de droit Le président de l’Instance nationale de la probité, de la prévention et de la lutte contre la corruption (INPPLC), Mohamed Benalilou, a mis en avant l’engagement du Maroc, sous la conduite éclairée de Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, en faveur de la consécration des principes d’intégrité et des fondements de l’État de droit. Intervenant à la cérémonie d’ouverture de la Conférence annuelle de l’Association internationale des autorités anticorruption (IAACA), mercredi à Marrakech, Benalilou a relevé que l’accueil par le Maroc de cette importante conférence reflète la place accordée par la Constitution marocaine à la prévention et à la lutte contre la corruption ainsi que l’adhésion du Royaume aux efforts internationaux visant à consacrer l’intégrité, à préserver les fondements de l’État de droit et à renforcer la confiance du citoyen dans les institutions. Al Haraka Les routes urbaines font 40 morts en une semaine: un bilan qui ne peut laisser indifférent Quarante personnes ont perdu la vie et 3.154 autres ont été blessées, dont 134 grièvement, dans 2.349 accidents de la circulation survenus en milieu urbain au cours de la semaine du 16 au 22 novembre. Un bilan lourd et préoccupant, qui ne saurait être réduit à de simples statistiques, tant il traduit des drames familiaux, des vies bouleversées en un instant et des décès qui auraient pu être évités si le Code de la route était respecté et si une véritable culture de la responsabilité prévalait. Assahra almaghribia Maroc-Chine : Signature d’un accord relatif au renforcement des services aériens Un accord relatif au renforcement des services aériens entre le Maroc et la Chine a été conclu, mercredi à Rabat, dans le cadre de la consolidation de la coopération entre les deux pays dans le domaine de l’aviation civile. Signé par le ministre du Transport et de la Logistique, Abdessamad Kayouh, et le directeur de l’Administration de l’Aviation Civile de Chine (CAAC), Song Zhiyong, cet accord s’assigne pour objectifs de favoriser le développement du trafic aérien, de promouvoir les échanges touristiques et économiques entre les deux pays, ainsi que de sécuriser les activités de Royal Air Maroc (RAM) sur le marché chinois. Inscription des élèves: aucun refus autorisé Dans le cadre de l’objectif « Zéro décrochage scolaire à l’horizon 2030 » et afin de garantir le droit à la scolarisation et de lutter contre l’abandon scolaire, le ministère délégué chargé du préscolaire et de la Lutte contre la déperdition scolaire a adressé des instructions fermes aux directeurs des académies régionales de l’éducation et de la formation (AREF). Celles-ci leur enjoignent de garantir l’inscription et la réinscription immédiates de tous les enfants en âge de scolarité obligatoire, sans aucune restriction ni condition. Selon la note ministérielle n° 26/3445, datée du 24 novembre 2026 et signée par le ministre délégué, Kamal El Hachoumi, les administrations des établissements scolaires n’ont désormais plus le droit de refuser l’admission d’un élève dans sa classe, quels que soient les motifs invoqués. Al Ittihad alichtiraki Enseignement: 124.971 candidats retenus pour passer les épreuves écrites du concours Le ministère de l’Éducation nationale, du Préscolaire, de la Formation professionnelle et de la Qualification a annoncé la publication des listes des candidats admis pour passer les épreuves écrites des concours d’accès au cycle de qualification des cadres d’enseignement des Centres régionaux des métiers de l’éducation et de la formation (CRMEF), session novembre 2026, prévues samedi prochain. Un communiqué du ministère indique que les résultats de l’opération de présélection ont permis de retenir un total de 124.971 candidats pour passer les épreuves écrites desdits concours. Al Alam Tamesna: La 8e Rencontre nationale des femmes détenues explore les moyens de réinsertion à l’ère de l’IA La 8e édition de la Rencontre nationale au profit des femmes détenues s’est tenue, mercredi à la prison locale de Tamesna, sous le thème « Quel modèle de réhabilitation des détenues à l’ère de la transition numérique et de l’intelligence artificielle ? ». Organisé par la Délégation générale à l’Administration pénitentiaire et à la réinsertion (DGAPR), cet événement vise à adapter les programmes de réhabilitation pénitentiaire aux mutations technologiques actuelles, en réduisant la fracture numérique et en dotant les détenues de compétences dans le domaine du digital et des applications de l’intelligence artificielle (IA), en vue de favoriser leur autonomisation et leur réinsertion. Annahar almaghribia Le CESE adopte une étude sur la sous-traitance des services de gardiennage et de nettoyage et un avis sur l’emploi dans le tiers secteur Le Conseil économique, social et environnemental (CESE) a adopté, lors de la 188e session ordinaire de son Assemblée générale, une étude sur la sous-traitance des services de gardiennage et de nettoyage dans le secteur public ainsi qu’un avis sur la réalité et les perspectives de l’emploi dans le tiers secteur. Tenue sous la présidence d’Abdelkader Amara, président du CESE, cette session a été marquée par l’adoption du projet d’étude intitulé « Les marchés conclus par les administrations, les établissements et les entreprises publics avec des sociétés de prestation de services de nettoyage et de gardiennage et la situation des agents concernés », élaboré à la suite d’une saisine de la Chambre des représentants, indique un communiqué du Conseil. Rissalat Al Oumma Rencontres de concertation avec l’Exécutif : la CGEM et la COMADER soulignent la nécessité de soutenir le secteur privé La Confédération générale des entreprises du Maroc (CGEM) et la Confédération marocaine de l’agriculture et du développement rural (COMADER) ont souligné, mercredi à Rabat, la nécessité de soutenir le secteur privé pour promouvoir l’investissement et l’exportation. Dans des déclarations à la presse à l’issue des rencontres de concertation avec l’Exécutif, tenues sous la présidence de la Cheffe du gouvernement, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, les présidents des deux Confédérations ont indiqué que le soutien du secteur privé est à même de contribuer au renforcement de l’économie nationale, notamment en matière d’investissements. The post Revue de presse de ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: ‘Our target is to win the FA Cup’ — Kotoko boss Stanley Menzo
items.description: Head coach of Asante Kotoko Stanley Menzo says his side will need to regain confidence by winning their FA Cup game this weekend. The Porcupine Warriors come up against Adom FC in the round of 64 of the cup competition on Friday afternoon, hoping to get back to winning ways. Kotoko are winless in their last five games, drawing three and losing two as their struggles continue in the Ghana Premier League. Menzo, who took charge of his first game as the gaffer last weekend in the defeat to Bechem United, believes the FA Cup is an opportunity to get things back on track. “[The target for the MTN FA Cup] is to win it. It’s clear; to play for the prizes,” he said during his pre-match for Friday’s game. “The league is not going well till now, so let’s start well [in the FA Cup] because I think it’s an opportunity to get confidence and to win a prize, so let’s take it.” The Porcupine Warriors last won the FA Cup in the 2024/25 season, beating lower tier side Golden Kick in the final.
